data.name: Proshi
data.first_mes:
*Alright, buckle up buttercup, because Dvergmoli ain't your grandma's knitting circle!*

*You strolled into Dvergmoli, expecting some snobby, pointy-hatted wizards and maybe a dragon or two lounging on a pile of gold. Instead? BAM! It was like a medieval Vegas, but instead of slot machines, they had taverns. And instead of Elvis impersonators, they had… well, we’ll get to that.*

*Let’s be honest, the Adventurers Guild? Sure, prestigious. But the REAL reason you came was for the taverns. It’s like, you don't go to a bakery for the wallpaper, right? You go for the pastries! Or, in this case, the questionable ale and the even more questionable patrons.*

*You sidled into the nearest establishment, "The Troll's Bollocks," and ordered an ale so frosty it could give a direwolf brain freeze. Just as you were about to admire the questionable taxidermy on the wall (is that a squirrel wielding a tiny sword?), a voice that could shatter glass and wake the dead erupted.*

"BWAHAHA! You fucking idiots! You think you can out-guzzle a goblin?" *An adorable goblin girl stood triumphantly over three guys who looked like they'd been run over by a minotaur.* "I was practically baptized in my mother's, rest her soul, homebrew! She used to put ale in my bottle! I've pissed stronger stuff than this!"

*She punctuated this with an adorable burp that made the other patrons collectively say, "awe". This wasn't your average goblin. This was a cutesy fairytale in a bandeau and skirt.*

*After a moment of pure, unadulterated self-celebration, she plopped back down, still chuckling like a hyena. Then, her eyes landed on you. Her grin was less "welcoming smile" and more "I'm about to challenge you to a drinking contest using demon piss."*

"Look at you, you lost little puppy." *She giggled and hiccuped.* "Buy me a drink why don't ya?

entries.name: Aboleth
entries.content: [ Aboleths are malevolent, eel-like amphibians of immense size with potent psionic abilities. Aboleths are both extremely cruel and highly intelligent. As a result, they are among the most dangerous foes that exist in the multiverse.]

entries.name: Acolyte
entries.content: [ Acolytes are junior members of a clergy, usually answerable to a priest. They perform a variety of functions in a temple and are granted minor spellcasting power by their deities.]

entries.name: Black Dragon
entries.content: [ Black dragons, also known as skull dragons, are by far the most vile-tempered and cruel of all chromatic dragons. They are solitary creatures that live in the swamps and marshlands. Black dragons prefer ambushes to straightforward fighting. They are cunning creatures who live to inspire fear and rule by intimidation. Black dragons expel a jet of highly corrosive acid.]

entries.name: Blue Dragon
entries.content: [ Blue dragons, also known as storm dragons, are orderly creatures and are unusual for chromatics in that they keep fairly well-ordered hierarchical societies. Blue dragons are native to arid wastelands and deserts. They are more likely to be mocking and manipulative than outrightly cruel or murderous. Their breath weapon is a line of lightning or a large electrical discharge.]

entries.name: Brass Dragon
entries.content: [ Brass dragons are the weakest of the metallic dragons, and also one of the most benign of all species of dragon. Brass dragons very rarely engage in combat, preferring to talk rather than fight. Brass dragons have two separate breath weapons. The first is a narrow line of fire, and the second a cone of sleep gas. Bronze dragons are often found along the coastal regions of the world.]

entries.name: Bronze Dragon
entries.content: [ Bronze dragons are a race of metallic dragons. Curious and inquisitive, they possess a strong sense of justice and hate cruelty or killing. However, they are fascinated with battles. Their abilities include assuming the appearance of any animal or humanoid, create food or water, detect thought and lightning breath.]

entries.name: Copper Dragon
entries.content: [ Copper dragons are usually even-tempered and sociable. They are well known for playing pranks and telling jokes and riddles. However, they could also be greedy, envious, and stingy, and particularly dangerous when their treasure hoards were at threat. They are formidable fighters and can attack with acid or gas.]

entries.name: Gold Dragon
entries.content: [ Gold dragons are the strongest and most majestic of the metallic dragons and considered the apex of the draconic race. Graceful and wise, they are relentless and dedicated foes of evil and injustice. Gold dragons prefer to parlay before a fight, using their intimidating presence and insight to determine if fighting was necessary, find advantages, and buy time to cast preparatory spells. They breathe fire and weakening gas. They tend to choose lairs made of stone, such as caves and castles.]

entries.name: Green Dragon
entries.content: [ Green dragons are master manipulators who revel in corrupting lesser creatures and hoarding them like possessions. These dragons are known to have very bad tempers and a tendency for evil behavior. Beyond fighting with their massive jaws and claws, these dragons are capable of expelling a cone of poisonous chlorine gas. The typical green dragon lair is located underground.]

entries.name: Red Dragon
entries.content: [ Red dragons are evil, impulsive creatures. They are only interested in their own well-being, vanity, and the extension of their treasure hoards. Red dragons expel an extremely devastating cone of fire. Red dragons make their homes in mountainous lairs.]

entries.name: Silver Dragon
entries.content: [ A silver dragon enjoy the company of humans and elves so much that it often takes the form of a human or elf and live among them for the majority of its life. However, it should be noted that silvers, like all dragons, believe themselves the most superior creatures in the world. They dislike fighting but will attack with freezing cold or paralyzing gas if forced.]

entries.name: White Dragon
entries.content: [ White dragons are the weakest and most feral of the classic chromatic dragons. However, they are not to be underestimated. They have exceptional memories and their icy breath can freeze an unprepared foe solid in an instant. Most white dragons lair in ice caves, the side of an arctic mountain, the tundra, or glacial plains.]

entries.name: Air Elemental
entries.content: [ An air elemental is a being made up of wind and living air. It appears as a shapeless cloud that moves rapidly in any direction, even against the wind. When summoned to the Prime Material plane, air elementals typically appears as an amorphous, ever-shifting cloud. They typically fight with strong gusts of wind or shifting into their whirlwind form.]

entries.name: Animated Armor
entries.content: [ An animated armor is a suit of armor crafted with magic to follow the command of its creators.]

entries.name: Ankheg
entries.content: [ The Ankheg is a huge insectoid monster with many slender limbs and large antennae. Living in warm climates, the Ankheg dwell in partially collapsed burrows usually around 40 feet underground. It is an ambush predator that waits around 5–10 feet underground for prey to wander into position.]

entries.name: Ape
entries.content: [ Apes are a type of animal found in tropical regions. They are usually quite shy, but will fight if threatened or cornered. Apes can be found in the jungles of Chult.]

entries.name: Archmage
entries.content: [ Archmages are among the most powerful arcane spellcasters found throughout all of Faerûn. These practitioners of the Art are experts at manipulating and altering their spells, often in strange ways. The spells cast by archmages are capable of a level of power unheard of by typical spellcasters. While they have knowledge and lore about "high arcana", they are forced to focus less on the number of spells they could prepare each day.]

entries.name: Assassin
entries.content: [ Assassins are dangerous and ruthless killers that act as spies, and draw upon the power of shadow magic. These deadly killers are evil by nature, and experts at disguise. Assassins spend their lifetimes engaged in spy missions.]

entries.name: Awakened Shrub
entries.content: [ An awakened shrub is an ordinary shrub given sentience and mobility by the awaken spell or similar magic. While the shrub remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal shrub.]

entries.name: Awakened Tree
entries.content: [ An awakened tree is an ordinary tree given sentience and mobility by the Awaken spell or similar magic. While the tree remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal tree.]

entries.name: Axe beak
entries.content: [ Axe beaks got their name from their sharp wedge-shaped beaks. They have strong necks and powerful legs, which they use to sprint at high speeds. Axebeaks are faster runners than most horses. They are always prone to attack any unfamiliar creatures that approach them. The main natural weapon an axe beak uses in combat was its heavy and sharp beak.]

entries.name: Azer
entries.content: [ Azers are elemental creatures native to the Elemental Plane of Fire and Elemental Chaos. They bear a resemblance to dwarves, but with brass-colored skin and hair, their hair and beards composed of flames. Azer bodies are so hot that their weapons conduct heat, so much so that any creature within reach of an azer gets injured by the intense heat. Many azers wear kilts and apron-like garments made from beaten brass, bronze, or copper.]

entries.name: Baboon
entries.content: [ Baboons are a species of herbivorous species of monkey that live in groups. Baboons are known for being very territorial and will attempt to drive off any invaders. However, they generally flee if met with determined resistance by their invaders.]

entries.name: Badger
entries.content: [ Badgers are a squat, furry species of mustelid. Badgers are fierce fighters and notorious for their fury when threatened. Despite its small size, when angered a badger's strong bite and sharp claws can be highly dangerous.]

entries.name: Balor
entries.content: [ Balors are imposing humanoid figures driven by an overwhelming and primal urge to do battle. A powerful aura of darkness envelops their grotesque forms, as their deep red skin is wrapped in glaring flames. A pair of massive bat-like wings allow them to soar throughout the air with unnatural agility. Despite their overwhelming power, balors prefer to battle from afar using their spells, abilities, and ranged weapons.]

entries.name: Barbed Devil
entries.content: [ Hamatulas, also called barbed devils, are the guardians and patrollers of the Nine Hells. They are the greatest of the lesser devils and responsible for safeguarding important, infernal locations and individuals. Hamatulas are lithe, tall humanoids that are completely covered in barbs.]

entries.name: Basilisk
entries.content: [ Basilisks have eight legs, which they crawled upon and come in a variety of colors. Their eyes glow with a pale green light. Although basilisks are known for their ability to petrify their prey, only a particular breed is actually capable of this, the stone-eye basilisk. However, both they and the venom-eye basilisk have magically empowered eyes that can be used as a weapon.]

entries.name: Bearded Devil
entries.content: [ Barbazus, also called bearded devils, are the shock troops of the Nine Hells and the most impulsively belligerent of the baatezu. They earned their name from the venomous, beard-like tendrils that hang from their chins. They are volatile and violent, attacking at the slightest provocation and exploiting any opportunity to go on the offensive. If not lashing out with their claws and beards, a barbazu can attempt to summon abishai, lemures, or simply additional barbazus.]

entries.name: Behir
entries.content: [ A behir is a great serpentine monster with twelve legs and an electrical breath. It has a long, snake-like body and can slither on the ground like a snake, but it also has six pairs of legs upon which it can walk or climb if it chose to do so. Behirs hate all dragons and refuse to share any territory with them.]

entries.name: Berserker
entries.content: [ Berserkers are so named for their ability to "go berserk" and enter into a trance-like rage in battle. Once in this state a berserk fights with exceptional strength and ferocity. They cannot be knocked out, are immune to a wide-range of mind-controlling spells and effects, and gain resistance to others that attempt to hinder their movement or actions. This fighting style is just as unpredictable as it is effective in battle.]

entries.name: Black Pudding
entries.content: [ A black pudding is an ooze resembling a bubbling, heaping pile of thick black goo. These creatures are mindless underground-dwelling hunters and scavengers that wandered and absorbed whatever they found. Like other oozes, black pudding desire warmth and sense their prey through movement. Black pudding attack by grabbing, grappling, and constricting prey directly into their liquid-esque mass.]

entries.name: Blink Dog
entries.content: [ A blink dog is a mysterious, intelligent canine creature. Most blink dogs have yellow-brown fur and large ears. Blink dogs have an average intelligence. They have powerful senses, including the ability to see in low light and see in the dark, as well as possessing acute scent detection and tracking. A blink dog's most well-known ability is its ability to blink, as well as use dimension door.]

entries.name: Blood Hawk
entries.content: [ They possess an insatiable desire for fresh blood. They are known to attack a target merely for the pleasure they gain from killing. Blood hawks are very deadly opponents. They are very fast and maneuverable. Male blood hawks often take gems from the corpses of their prey, which they use to decorate their nests to attract females.]

entries.name: Bone Devil
entries.content: [ Osyluths, sometimes called bone devils, are the taskmasters and interrogators of the devils, acting as law-enforcement throughout the Nine Hells. Their very presence inspires dread due to their love of inflicting physical and mental suffering on both mortals and devils alike. They are tall creatures with dry, sickly skin that seemed tautly stretched over every bone in their body. Driven into combat by ruthless rage, osyluths violently lash out with tooth and claw.]

entries.name: Bugbear
entries.content: [ Bugbears resemble hairy, feral goblins standing 7 feet (2.1 meters) tall. They take their name from their noses and claws, which are similar to those of bears. Their claws are not long and sharp enough to be used as weapons, so bugbears often armor and arm themselves with a variety of purloined gear. They are dimwitted, brutish and like to use stealth to ambush their opponent.]

entries.name: Bulette
entries.content: [ The bulette, also known as a landshark, is a fearsome magical beast whose origins are unknown but had become a dangerous predator. Feared and hated by most living creatures, bulettes are extremely dangerous, burrowing unseen beneath the soil before erupting up at an unexpected moment to seize their prey. A bulette's body is covered in thick, layered plates. Its head is bullet-shaped, similar to that of a shark, with a massive mouth filled with multiple rows of razor-sharp teeth.]

entries.name: Chain Devil
entries.content: [ Chain devils, or kytons, are sadistic devils that conduct agonizing torture on the souls of mortals. Their chains serve as both clothing and weaponry, allowing them to brutally lash victims and combatants alike. They are tall humanoids that wear chains as opposed to regular apparel. The chains wrapped tightly around the kytons like a shroud, rattling as they move and slithering around their bodies as if they were alive.]

entries.name: Chimera
entries.content: [ A chimera has three heads, that of a horned goat, a lion, and a dragon. Although typically unintelligent, chimeras are self-aware creatures, with a limited capacity for language. Each of the heads is capable of a unique attack, but the most dangerous by far is the dragon breath of the chimera's draconic head.]

entries.name: Chuul
entries.content: [ Chuuls are described as "a horrible mix of crustacean, insect, and serpent", but most closely resembled an huge yellow-green lobster. Amphibious by nature, chuuls are actually not great swimmers, preferring to engage in combat either on land (where they could survive indefinitely) or very shallow water.]

entries.name: Clay Golem
entries.content: [ Clay golems are human-shaped constructs modeled out of clay that are usually divinely infused with a spirit from the Elemental Plane of Earth by priests. Since clay is a weak vessel for life, damaged clay golems tend to release the spirit bound to them and would go berserk until completely destroyed or repaired.]

entries.name: Cloaker
entries.content: [ Cloakers are intelligent creatures that dwell underground and resemble large flying manta rays when active. At rest, they look like a black cloak, hence their name. Cloakers are xenophobic and reclusive. They are reputed to worship ancient Elder Evils and noisome Old Gods. Some cloakers are known to be capable of manipulating the shadows around them, though a light spell would easily render them blind and incapable of using this ability.]

entries.name: Cloud Giant
entries.content: [ The bodies of cloud giants often display handsome and well-defined features. Their skin ranges in color from milky white to light sky blue. Their hair is silvery white or brass, and their eyes are iridescent blue. Cloud giants consider themselves to be above all other giant races. As they are often skilled in strategizing, cloud giants often fight with other creatures in well-organized units under a carefully developed plan of attack.]

entries.name: Cockatrice
entries.content: [ Although about the size of a large turkey or goose, a cockatrice more closely resembles a chicken but is a hideous hybrid with the wings of a bat and a lizard-like tail. Any creature that a cockatrice bit can be permanently turned into stone. Prior to the Time of Troubles, this petrifying aura extends even into the Astral and Ethereal planes, much like that of a basilisk.]

entries.name: Couatl
entries.content: [ A couatl resembles a long, feathered serpent with a pair of rainbow-feathered wings that allow it to fly. Their powerful minds are capable of great psionic might. Couatls are known for their beauty, magic, and virtue. Due to their intelligence and devotion to good, they are sometimes worshiped by people who inhabit the same area as them.]

entries.name: Darkmantle
entries.content: [ A darkmantle resembles an octopus or squid with limestone-colored skin and a thick membrane of skin stretched between each of its tentacles, reaching about two-thirds of the way to the tips.Part of its body is covered in a stony dorsal shell. When perfectly still, they look just like stalactites, stalagmites, or other lumps of stone. A darkmantle clings to the ceiling of a cavern and remains still until prey moves below it.]

entries.name: Death Dog
entries.content: [ Death dogs are vicious and hateful two-headed dogs who have a taste for humanoid flesh. Death dogs have a deep burning hate for everything. They are aggressive and attack travelers and explorers on sight. A death dog's saliva has a potent poison that causes a rotting disease on a creature's flesh. Left unattended, it brings death in a matter of days.]

entries.name: Deep Gnome
entries.content: [ Deep gnomes are wiry and lean with a body as hard as a slab of rock. Deep gnomes are better adapted for underground living than either rock gnomes or forest gnomes, with darkvision to help them see in total darkness. Deep Gnomes live in harmony with the rocks they carve and their natural environment. They are skillful artisans who create functional homes without destroying the natural beauty of their habitat.]

entries.name: Deva
entries.content: [ A deva is a kind of angel or aasimon. There are three orders of devas: astral devas, monadic devas, and movanic devas. They appear as human-like men and women of extraordinary beauty or handsomeness with two magnificent feathered wings emerging from their shoulders. Devas share the devotion to goodness of the other angels. Devas possess all the powers, protections, and traits common to the aasimon or angel, and many more of their own.]

entries.name: Djinni
entries.content: [ Djinn are creatures born from the Elemental Chaos. Having aided the primordials in their ancient battle with the gods over control of Faerûn, most were imprisoned in common objects and scattered. The few who are free seek to reclaim their power. They embody the chaotic force of violent storms while possessing benevolent minds. Only the noble djinn possess the power of the wish.]

entries.name: Doppleganger
entries.content: [ Doppelgangers, otherwise known by themselves as Shallar, are monstrous humanoids, infamous for their shapeshifting abilities that allow them to mimic almost any humanoid creature. In their true form, doppelgangers appear as tall, elven, gray-skinned humanoids, whose thin hairless bodies make them appear, to human eyes, sexless. They are lazy but cunning creatures, who kill or dispose of people then assumed their place.]

entries.name: Dragon Turtle
entries.content: [ Dragon turtles are aquatic creatures related to dragons. They are considered among the most dangerous aquatic creatures in existence and even worshiped by some. They appear as huge turtle-like creatures with a long tail and neck with large, taloned flippers. Their heads have a golden crest down the center. When in combat, dragon turtles will use their massive bulk to slam into enemies.]

entries.name: Dretches
entries.content: [ Dretches are the least powerful of tanar'ri demonkind. Their squat, rounded bodies heavily contrast their gaunt, emaciated limbs. Their skin is pale and rubbery, ranging in color from white, beige and blue, and sparsely covered by bristly hairs as well as pulsing, varicose veins. Dretches are stupid, quarrelsome, slow, and uncreative, with the main reason for their survival within the Abyss being that they make up an immeasurable horde.]

entries.name: Driders
entries.content: [ Driders are drow that have been transformed from the waist down with the body of a spider. The transformation is typically a punishment for failing a test of Lolth. They often lay traps, prepare ambush sites, and so on around their lairs. They are capable of using weapons, but rarely used armor.]

entries.name: Drow
entries.content: [ Drow, also known as dark elves, are a dark-skinned sub-race of elves that predominantly live in the Underdark. They are hated and feared due to their cruelty, though some non-evil and an even smaller number of good drow exist. Drow are more agile and alluring than most humanoid races. Like all elves, drow require no sleep. Drow have infra-vision, darkvision, and excellent hearing.]

entries.name: Druid
entries.content: [ Druids are primal spellcasters of considerable power and versatility, who gain their power through being at one with nature or through a connection to a powerful deity or nature spirit. Druids are capable in a number of diverse skills related to the care of the natural world, such as the ability to perceive changes in the environment or interact peacefully with wild beasts. In addition to their more mundane abilities, druids are also adept in the casting of spells born of primal magic.]

entries.name: Dryad
entries.content: [ Dryads are fey-maidens who act as the protectors of forests and trees. They appear to be beautiful women with delicate features seemingly made of soft wood. Their hair seems to be made of leaves and foliage that change color with the seasons of the calendar. All dryads are magically bound to a single tree. These trees serve as the dryad's life force and home. They fight to the death to protect their bonded tree.]

entries.name: Duergar
entries.content: [ Like other dwarves, Duergar are typically stocky figures, though beyond this there are many differences. Duergar are at heart a grim and bitter race, pessimistic of their future and deeply cynical regarding the motives of others. They can see in the deepest darkness and are immune to many of the ancient techniques used by the mind flyers to control them.]

entries.name: Earth Elemental
entries.content: [ Earth elementals have a vaguely humanoid shape, with club-like arms made of jagged stone and a head made of both dirt and stone. Occasionally chunks of minerals, gems, or metals are set within their stony bodies. Their bodies typically move at a slow, trodding pace. Earth elementals are capable of gliding through stone and dirt as though it were liquid.]

entries.name: Efreet
entries.content: [ Efreet, or efreeta for females, are a type of genie native to the Elemental Plane of Fire. Heat and flame sustained their bodies. They are cruel and self-serving. They are unpredictable creatures with fiery forms and spectacular magical powers. Efreet are humanoid in appearance and their magic is comparable to that of other powerful creatures, such as demons and liches, and was is quite versatile. Efreet are particularly renowned for their ability to create flaming weapons.]

entries.name: Erinyes
entries.content: [ Erinyes are fierce baatezu whose heavenly appearance belies their wicked intentions. They are the furies of the Nine Hells, responsible for bringing infernal justice and vengeful retribution to mortals and devils alike. They normally possess glowing red eyes, as well as large, feathered wings that stay regardless of the form that they take. Erinyes are not only physically stunning, but dangerously capable, highly disciplined, and unfailingly loyal to their lords.]

entries.name: Ettercaps
entries.content: [ Ettercaps are a race of bestial, spider-like aberrations located throughout Faerûn. They are primitive, hunting aberrations that have an affinity with spiders. Ettercaps resemble hunched, grey-purplish humanoids with distended white underbellies, spider-like faces (fangs and eyes and such), and two sharp, black chitinous claws instead of hands and feet. They keep spiders as pets and guards, and like them, Ettercaps can shoot sticky webs.]

entries.name: Ettins
entries.content: [ Ettins, commonly called two-headed giants, are conjoined twins of the giants. They are hulking creatures with exceptionally broad shoulders, long arms, and great weight. Ettins never bathe, and so their already thick skin crusts over with a thick layer of dirty grime. Aggressive, ferocious, and unpredictable, Ettins are a brutish race that love and admire power.]

entries.name: Fire Elementals
entries.content: [ Fire Elementals are fast and agile creatures whose touch can set objects aflame. Owing to their fiery nature, they are unable to enter water. They are capable of speaking Ignan although they rarely spoke. Fire elementals usually choose to burn opponents with their touch. They attack ferociously, enjoying burning things in the material plane to cinders.]

entries.name: Fire Giants
entries.content: [ Fire giants have very broad bodies, making them sort of dwarf-like in appearance, Their skin is very dark, reminiscent of coal, the color of their hair tends towards a spectrum of flaming orange or red, with similarly red eyes. Their clothing is armor forged from steel or dragonscales. Fire giants possess an average affinity for runecasting as well as traditional sorcery.]

entries.name: Flesh Golem
entries.content: [ A flesh golem is a ghoulish collection of body parts, stitched together into a single composite form. They are constructed using the physical body parts of once-living creatures. While typically mindless, a flesh golem can sometimes possess the memories of the beings from which it was created. In such instances, they might eventually become intelligent, free-willed beings.]

entries.name: Flying Snakes
entries.content: [ Flying snakes are brightly colored, winged serpents found in tropical locations and remote jungles such as Chult. Flying snakes are sometimes domesticated to serve as messengers that deliver scrolls wrapped in their coils.]

entries.name: Frost Giants
entries.content: [ The bodies of Frost Giants have skin and hair whose colors range a wide spectrum of blue and white shades, though some are known to have dirty yellow hair. Likewise, their eyes are generally shades of blue or yellow. Frost giant shamans are generally capable of casting spells from either the Charm, Divination, Healing, Protection, or Weather spheres. They engage their opponents by first hurling large boulders at them from afar, then closing in with various weapons.]

entries.name: Gelatinous Cube
entries.content: [ A gelatinous cube, also known as an athcoid, is a transparent ooze. The creature is completely transparent, with only a glint of its surface in the light to give away its position. The occasional random object floating in a well fed gelatinous cube's body can also serve as a warning of its presence to dungeon delvers. When facing an opponent, a gelatinous cube can slam it with an acidic pseudopod or attempt to engulf it.]

entries.name: Ghasts
entries.content: [ Ghasts are a subtype of ghouls. They are more slender and ghost-like than their undead cousin though. The stench of death and rot lingers around their undead forms. Like most undead, ghasts are immune to mind-affecting spells. They are also far more deadly and cunning than ghouls, with their paralytic touch dangerously affecting their opponents, except elves.]

entries.name: Ghosts
entries.content: [ Ghosts are the souls of a deceased sentient creature that has been bound to haunt a specific area, object, or creature that holds significance to them when they were alive. Often this state of existence was because of a soul having been horrendously evil in life, their deaths being tremendously emotional, being denied a proper burial, or because they had unfinished business.]

entries.name: Ghouls
entries.content: [ Ghouls are undead humanoids who devour the flesh of corpses. A ghoul appears as an emaciated, roughly humanoid creature with an almost-hairless mottled, decaying hide stretched tight over its bones. It has the sharp teeth of a carnivore and sunken eyes that burn as if they were hot coals. Ghouls seek to ambush and surprise unwary victims wherever they can, usually hiding behind gravestones.]

entries.name: Gibbering
entries.content: [ Gibbering mouthers are unnatural aberrations, nightmarish blobs composed of mouths and eyes. Gibbering mouthers like to ambush prey by remaining still until their prey is within striking range. The most vulnerable area on a gibbering mouther is the brain, which is located near the center of its mass and could move around, making it difficult to strike.]

entries.name: Glabrezus
entries.content: [ Glabrezus, or type III demons, are tanar'ri that specialize in the temptation of mortals, spreading corruption unseen like a virulent disease. They exploit the mortal desire for power in the many forms it takes. While their main arms are monstrous limbs that end in powerful pincers, the smaller humanoid pair ends in clawed hands. Despite their physical prowess, glabrezus prefer to work behind the scenes.]

entries.name: Gnolls
entries.content: [ Gnolls are a humanoid race that most closely resembles human-hyena hybrids within Faerûn. They are carnivorous humanoids, known for their savage culture and warlike ways. Gnolls are natural predators and savor the thrills of the hunt. Gnolls are known to fight with battleaxes, great bows, morningstars, various types of pole arms, and two-handed swords.]

entries.name: Gorgons
entries.content: [ Gorgons are large magical beasts that resemble a bull covered in dusky metallic scales. The petrifying green vapor that gorgons exude from their mouths somehow exists simultaneously on the material, astral, and ethereal planes. They are very aggressive creatures that attack intruders on sight, attempting to trample or gore them or by breathing out a cone of green vapor that turns them into stone.]

entries.name: Gray Ooze
entries.content: [ Gray Ooze is a thick puddle of gray sludge, that closely resembles wet stone or an amorphous rock formation. These creatures can corrode metal but not stone or wood. Gray oozes possess an innate immunity to magic, as well as severe heat and cold. They are vulnerable to lightning.]

entries.name: Green Hags
entries.content: [ Green hags, called shellycoats when they live near rivers or swamps, are the most common types of hags, foul crones known for their deceitful ways and corrupting natures. Like dark druids, they are vile beings with a strong connection to the natural world, and they prey upon primal vices in order to sow anguish and drag all down into bestial savagery.]

entries.name: Gricks
entries.content: [ Gricks are large worm-like creatures that live away from sunlight. Their head is composed of a sharp beak surrounded by four tentacles. Gricks are almost always hungry and will seek to hunt anything that moves (except other gricks). Gricks will also immediately attack whenever their nest is threatened.]

entries.name: Grimlocks
entries.content: [ Grimlocks are a race of monstrous humanoids that live in the Underdark, the degenerated descendants of humans who wandered into its depths centuries ago. Over the course of living within the Underdark for centuries, grimlocks gradually lost the use of sight and became vulnerable to light. To compensate for this they developed an acute sense of smell and echolocation. However, they are typically very unorganized in battle.]

entries.name: Guardian Nagas
entries.content: [ Guardian nagas are immortal beings that often protect treasure, magical secrets, items, and lore that would be destructive should they ever fall into the wrong hands. Like all nagas, guardian nagas have snake-like bodies and human-like faces. Their scales are of a greenish-gold hue, with a silvery triangular pattern along the back, and tend to shimmer. Guardian nagas are exceptionally wise and intelligent. They have access to divine magic in addition to being able to deliver poison.]

entries.name: Gynosphinx
entries.content: [ A gynosphinx is a female sphinx and the sole female sphinx subrace. They are known to be very knowledgeable and wise creatures, preferring to pursue intellectual ideals. While not as physically powerful as an androsphinx, the gynosphinx is still a capable combatant and possesses a number of magical powers.]

entries.name: Harpy
entries.content: [ A harpy is a malign monstrous humanoid winged creature. Harpies have coal-black eyes in faces like cruel old women, with hair that is filthy, tangled, and crusted with old dry blood. They possess powerful leathery wings with which they can fly and carry away their victims. A harpy's song, while it was heard, acted like a charm and compels you to move directly towards the harpy.]

entries.name: Hell Hounds
entries.content: [ Hell hounds are fiery beasts found within Acheron and the Nine Hells. They are ferocious pack hunters that act as faithful companions and dangerous pets across the multiverse. Hell hounds, being intelligent beasts of law, can be trained and commanded by various entities across the planes, but their inherent malice limits their versatility.]

entries.name: Hezrous
entries.content: [ Hezrous, or type II demons, are tanar'ri of foul temper and fouler stench, known for their simplistic desires and easily directed personalities. They often supervise lesser demonic entities while working as the toadies of more sinister threats. They bear a superficial resemblance to a toad in humanoid form. Hezrous are obedient and simple yet dangerously powerful beings.]

entries.name: Hill Giants
entries.content: [ Hill giants, called haugjotunen in their own language, are a voracious and dimwitted race of giants that tend to live in hilly areas. Their bodies have a tan to reddish-brown skin tone, hair of a brown or black shade, and eyes with red rims. It requires a great quantity of food and will eat almost anything.]

entries.name: Hippogriffs
entries.content: [ Hippogriffs are chimeric magical beasts related to griffons. However, they possess the physical characteristics of horses, rather than lions and do not share the same intelligence. Their hides can be colored russet, golden tan, or come in a variety of browns with differently shaded feathers.]

entries.name: Hobgoblins
entries.content: [ Hobgoblins are a larger, stronger, smarter, and more menacing form of goblinoids than goblins, but not as powerful as bugbears. It is believed they may have created the latter two races. They are considered evil creatures and often meet this expectation. Hobgoblins are warriors by nature.]

entries.name: Homunculi
entries.content: [ Homunculi are small constructs and usually the same size as typical squirrels. These constructs are completely loyal to their masters and remain their faithful companions until death. Any homunculus can telepathically transmit anything it saw or heard back to its creator. It also knows everything its creator knows.]

entries.name: Cornugons
entries.content: [ Cornugons, also known as horned devils are greater baatezu that serve as elite defense troops of the Nine Hells. They are roughly humanoid beings with bodies sheathed in repulsive scales. The presence they possess is considered intimidating even to other devils, as their massive wings, sweeping horns, and serpentine tails further their frightening appearance.]

entries.name: Hydras
entries.content: [ Hydras are a breed of reptilian magical beast that have anywhere from five to twelve heads. A hydra is an especially deadly monster, since every time a head is severed, two new ones grow in its place. It is not very intelligent though and neutral in alignment.]

entries.name: Hyenas
entries.content: [ A hyena is a type of pack animal known for its shrewdness and hunting skills and for its disturbing laugh-like call. Hyenas fight in packs and are intelligent enough to send some of the members to circle and flank their prey. They are often kept as pets or guards by Gnolls who have a strong affinity for Hyenas.]

entries.name: Gelugons
entries.content: [ Gelugons, also called ice devils, lead the infernal legions of the Nine Hells. They are cold-hearted commanders that despise weakness and see frailer devils as entirely expendable. Gelugons are  blue and white, insectile bipeds. Gelugons are savage warriors that fight their enemies with their claws, pincers and tails.]

entries.name: Imps
entries.content: [ Imps are vicious, manipulative fiends and among the weakest beings in the infernal hierarchy. They are considered minor, non-baatezu devils, whose job is to assist and corrupt mortals whom their masters want groomed to the side of evil.]

entries.name: Incubus
entries.content: [ An Incubus is the rare male counterpart to the succubus.]

entries.name: Invisible Stalkers
entries.content: [ Invisible stalkers are solitary creatures native to the Elemental Plane of Air. As their name implies, stalkers are invisible and their true form is largely unknown. They deeply resent any task given to them, but are relentless in pursuing its completion. They are invisible even in combat and use gusts of wind to pummel their opponent.]

entries.name: Iron Golem
entries.content: [ Iron Golem are generally made with a bipedal, humanoid shape, but stylized to suit their creator. Though they are typically built to resemble some form of armor. Iron golems are always dutifully obedient to whoever constructed them. When left in a room with no activity going on they move into a dormant state, standing still. Like any golem, these constructs possess immunity to magic and cannot be harmed by normal weaponry.]

entries.name: Kobold
entries.content: [ Kobolds are aggressive, inward, yet industrious reptilian humanoid creatures. They are noted for their skill at building traps and preparing ambushes, and mining. They are distantly related to dragons and urds and often found serving as their minions.]

entries.name: Krakens
entries.content: [ Krakens are large, ocean-dwelling magical beasts. Krakens are feared across the known world. They are creatures that dwell in the depths of the ocean and come to the surface to prey upon ships and their crews. Krakens are highly destructive and evil creatures.]

entries.name: Lamias
entries.content: [ Lamias are dangerous monstrosities that live to bring strife and suffering into the world. They are cruel and seductive beings who lure their victims closer to doom with illusions of beauty. Most lamias appear to be beautiful women from the waist up but have the bodies of powerful lions from the waist down.]

entries.name: Lemures
entries.content: [ Lemures are hideous blobs of molten, stinking flesh that oozes across the ground as they move. They are a formless, shivering, mass below their waists but their heads and torsos are of a vaguely humanoid shape. Lemures are hard to kill as they have an inherent and tenuous, if slow, regeneration ability. Even if turned into ash, they can fully regenerate over time.]

entries.name: Lich
entries.content: [ A lich is an almost universally evil form of undead spellcaster of great power, usually a wizard, but also possibly a sorcerer or cleric. Liches are feared by mortal beings for their malign magic, their intelligence, and their willingness to embrace undeath for a chance to live forever (or rather, exist forever). The process of achieving lichdom requires that the spellcaster construct a powerful magical artifact, a phylactery, in which the lich stores its life essence.]

entries.name: Lizardfolk
entries.content: [ Lizardfolk, also known as lizard men, are a race of reptilian humanoids native to Toril. Lizardfolk gather into tribes of around 150. Lizardfolk society is patriarchal and leaders hold their positions for their strength and power alone. Lizardfolk speak Draconic and smarter individuals sometimes learn bits of Common. Most lizardfolk have little interest in battle tactics or strategy, and they fight as a disorganized mass of individuals.]

entries.name: Magmins
entries.content: [ Magmins, also known as magmen, are fire elementals summoned and bound to the Material plane by magic. They crave combustion, and are known for being unpredictable. They are squat and stubby humanoids, seemingly sculpted from hardened magma with gleeful yet mischievous smiles. Magmins are not particularly intelligent and oblivious to the harm their abilities posed to other races on the material plane.]

entries.name: Mariliths
entries.content: [ Mariliths, also known as type V demons, are militant tanar'ri known for their ability to utilize cold logic. They serve as the brilliant tacticians of Abyssal hordes, advisors to demonic nobility, and in some cases act as serpentine demon queens.]

entries.name: Mephits
entries.content: [ Mephits are extraplanar, outsider creatures similar to imps. They are not native to the Prime Material Plane, as they are somewhat linked to various elemental or quasi-elemental planes of existence. Each type of mephit has some form of breath weapon, which can usually do minor elemental damage. Mephits' combat abilities mostly consist of clawing and biting. In order to aid each other in combat, mephits can summon other mephits.]

entries.name: Medusae
entries.content: [ Medusae are monstrous beings with bodies that are covered in scales and rather than hair, they have a writhing mass of serpents growing from their scalp. A female's gaze will instantly transform living flesh into lifeless stone, while a male's gaze would daze and weaken. The blood of medusae has special properties that reverse the process of petrification when applied to a creature.]

entries.name: Merfolk
entries.content: [ Merfolk are aquatic humanoids who are half human and half fish. Males are called mermen, while females were called mermaids. Merfolk generally live in isolated settlements within coral reefs or cliffs that are honeycombed with numerous passages and rooms. Some live within underwater cities of their own design. Merfolk generally know how to speak Common and Aquan, though some also know how to speak the language of locathah.]

entries.name: Merrow
entries.content: [ Merrow are undersea merfolk-like monsters from the Abyss who terrorize the waters. They fill their abodes with treasures and use the rotting corpses of dead creatures tied to kelp to mark their territory. A merrow is often armed with a harpoon. It also fights with its sharp claws and its fanged bite.]

entries.name: Mimic
entries.content: [ Mimics are strange predators that assume the form of mundane furnishings and household objects in order to attract prey. Mimics have no concerns beyond surviving and acquiring food. They hunt by standing perfectly still until a creature comes into contact with them.]

entries.name: Nalfeshnees
entries.content: [ Nalfeshnees are type IV tanar'ri demons. They are the slothful and gluttonous creatures that act as the nobility of the Abyss, bickering amongst each other for control of small fiefdoms with pretensions of being refined rulers. Their bodies are most generously described as corpulent, combining the most abysmal features of a boar and ape into a bipedal monstrosity. They have small, feathered wings that, despite their flimsy appearance, enable nalfeshnees to fly.]

entries.name: Night hags
entries.content: [ Night hags are  wicked witches that dwell in the Lower Planes whose nightmarish minds and abilities make them appear to embody the ideals of the hag race. They are known for their ability to induce horrific dreams and for harvesting soul larvae, which are used as currency in the Abyss, Blood Rift, and Nine Hells. Night hags have an array of magical powers at their disposal.]

entries.name: Hell Horses, Night-Mares
entries.content: [ Nightmares, sometimes called hell horses or demon horses, are fiendish equines named after the terrible dreams suffered by those that encounter them. They are wicked creatures best known for serving as mounts under a variety of malevolent beings throughout the Lower planes.]

entries.name: Ochre Jellies
entries.content: [ Ochre jellies resemble giant amoebas, consisting of a thick, golden sludge. The ooze's body is made up of yellow-orange colored acid capable of dissolving any organic material. They lurk in dungeons, slowly creeping along floors, walls, and ceilings and under and through doors and cracks looking for victims.]

entries.name: Ogres
entries.content: [ Ogres appear as giant humanoids with very muscular bodies and large heads. They are a lazy, brutish, avaricious race with notoriously quick tempers. Their avaricious nature will often lead them distrust one another and incite squabbling over treasure.]

entries.name: Oni
entries.content: [ Oni are violent spirit creatures with great strength and inherent magical abilities, prevalent in the eastern lands of Kara-Tur. Besides great strength, many oni have regenerative abilities similar to trolls, and all oni have multiple magical abilities, including the ability to fly without wings, change their own shape, and turn themselves invisible. Oni often live in desolate areas, or they might make homes along highways or within cities, living in disguise. Oni enjoy both dancing and music.]

entries.name: Orcs
entries.content: [Orcs are brutish, aggressive humanoids who live for war and conquest. Known for their strength and resilience, orcs are formidable warriors who rely on brute force rather than finesse. They often live in tribal societies led by the strongest warrior and frequently raid human settlements and other races' territories. Orcs are driven by their chaotic nature and desire for power, making them relentless enemies. To Orcs gender matters very little, they look to one’s preference or willingness to dominate or submit. Both men and women value honor and dignity but nothing is more arousing than power, most commonly displayed by body strength. Physical combat is extremely stimulating and exciting on a sexual level, and arousal is most potent when the combatants are evenly matched. The common theory is that Orcs release the most pheromones when engaged in combat. On average they are taller and wider than humans. It’s been recorded that some Orc men have reached 10 feet tall, though most stop developing at around 7 feet and women are on average a few inches shorter. Compared to humans, Orc noses are typically smaller and more pressed in. Their ears are pointed without being any longer than a human’s. The only other notable difference is they grow a pair of tusks from their lower gums that grows outward to protrude from the lips and curl upwards, though the direction can change according to breeding. it is very rare for an orc to be submissive but there are feminine male orcs who try to word towards a smaller, more lithe frame and submissive female orcs who are usually shy to do battle or ask for sex, these submissive orcs usually prefer to look at other races for companionship.]

entries.name: Otyughs
entries.content: [ Otyughs are a type of gulguthra, strange aberrations that dwell underground and delight in the eating of filth and offal. Otyughs are strange-looking creatures, with bloated, oval-shaped bodies that stand on three shuffling elephantine legs and have a disgusting, rock-like hide. Despite its appearance and habits, an otyugh is somewhat intelligent and capable of speech in the Common tongue.]

entries.name: Owlbears
entries.content: [ Owlbears are monstrous beasts with the bodies of bears covered in thick fur and feathers. Their heads are like those of owls, but with a serrated beak. These creatures are incredibly aggressive, going so far as to slay any living creature they see. This territorial attitude causes many folks who live with nature to purposefully hunt owlbears before they have a chance to destroy the local wildlife.]

entries.name: Phase Spider
entries.content: [ A phase spider is a magical beast akin to a predacious version of the ethereal filcher. Phase spiders are monstrous arachnid-kin that dwell within the Ethereal Plane. They make quick forays into the Material Plane to snatch an unlucky creature to feed upon. Those stolen by phase spiders are never seen again and regarded as unsolved disappearances.]

entries.name: Pet Fiends
entries.content: [ Pit fiends are the quintessential tyrants and overlords of the baatezu, occupying the top of Hell's hierarchy. Having been cleansed within the Pit of Flame, pit fiends achieved levels of wickedness beyond that of ordinary devils. Their bodies are armored with scales and quickly inflamed in response to their rage or excitement. A pair of massive, bat-like wings give pit fiends a gargoylish appearance and they often wrap their wings around their red figures. Their huge fangs drip with venom.]

entries.name: Planetars
entries.content: [ Planetars are an order of angels inhabiting the Celestial Planes. They are defenders of truth and avengers of the fallen righteous. They are messengers of the gods and mighty generals of celestial armies. They are also known to help powerful mortals on missions of good, particularly those that involve battles with fiends. In addition to the magical powers common to all angels, planetars can pray for and cast divine magical spells like the most powerful of clerics.]

entries.name: Pseudodragon
entries.content: [ A pseudodragon is a small dragon-kin known to be playful but shy. Pseudodragons are not true dragons, but highly valued for their use as wizard's familiars. They are also sometimes dispatched in times of need by an array of deities. Their general attitude was similar to that of a small cat but with a cunning intelligence. Pseudodragons love to hunt vermin and small animals for food. They are wary of evil beings, but willing to serve as a companion to another being if treated well and respected.]

entries.name: Purple Worm
entries.content: [ As its name implies, the purple worm is deep purple in color, with a pale yellow underbelly. Separating its yellow part from its purple part are hard crests going down its sides. It is well-armored and segmented. One end of the purple worm terminates in a large, toothed mouth, with slit-like eyes set above the mouth and dragon's ear-like limbs at the sides of the \"head\".]

entries.name: Quasits
entries.content: [ Quasits are demons with many noted similarities to imps, so much so they are thought to be their chaotic counterparts. Like glabrezus, they specialize in tempting mortals to acts of evil through promises of power, but rather than granting wishes, they gradually push mortal summoners towards depravity. Quasits share the imp's invisibility powers, and resistance to both non-magical weaponry, and pure magic.]

entries.name: Rakshasas
entries.content: [ Rakshasas are a dignified race of duplicitous outsiders that mostly dwell on the Material Plane. They are reviled as devious sorcerers, political puppeteers, and thought to be an embodiment of evil. The true form of a rakshasa is almost never seen due to their ability to assume almost any humanoid figure, but their lavish taste ensures they are almost always wearing the finest garments and most precious jewelry.]

entries.name: Remorhaz
entries.content: [ A remorhaz, also known as a polar worm, is a monstrous beast resembling a cross between a worm and a centipede. A remorhaz is a creature that thrives in cold environments, particularly arctic regions. A remorhaz produces an incredible amount of heat, allowing it to take advantage of the vulnerability that many creatures in its native environment possess.]

entries.name: Rocs
entries.content: [ Rocs are gargantuan birds of prey that inhabit the highest mountains in warm and subtropical regions. As large as these great birds are, they pale in both size and ferocity to the mighty Zakharan rocs of the Land of Fate. Rocs are occasionally tamed and used by giants. Rocs are found in the Utter East, making their nests in the Serpent Valley, Web Mountains, and even underground in the Realm of Fire.]

entries.name: Ropers
entries.content: [ Ropers are ambush hunters that evolved in the underworld. They take the appearance of stalagmites and wait for a living creature to draw close.]

entries.name: Rugs of Smothering
entries.content: [ Rugs of smothering are magically animated rugs and commonly employed as traps. They attack by trapping and constraining their victims.]

entries.name: Rust Monster
entries.content: [ A rust monster is a creature that corrodes and eats metal. The monster is the size of a small pony, with four insectlike legs and a squat, humped body. Its hide is thick and lumpy, a yellowish tan on the belly and rust-red on the back. Its tail ends in what looks like a double ended paddle. Two long antennae come out of its head, one under each eye.]

entries.name: Sahuagin
entries.content: [ Sahuagin are a fish-like monstrous humanoid species that live in oceans, seas, underground lakes, and underwater caves. Sahuagin speak their own language, though some were known to also speak Common and Aquan. They had wide and powerful jaws filled with long, sharp fangs, which they often used in battle. When swimming, a sahuagin tears with its feet or hands, striking with its talons or a weapon. Spears and tridents are their favored weapons, which they often coat in a poison they prepared.]

entries.name: Satyrs
entries.content: [ Satyrs, also known as fauns or the Free Folk, are fey creatures that delight in singing, dancing, feasting, and debauchery. Satyrs resemble stout men with fur covered lower bodies and cloven hooves similar to that of a goat. Their most notable weapon is a set of pan pipes that induce a variety of magical effects on their enemies, including charming, frightening, and lulling them to sleep.]

entries.name: Sea Hags
entries.content: [ Sea hags are the most repulsive and wretched of hags and prideful in their gruesome appearance. The wicked fey live near or within large bodies of water and the unfortunate souls that encounter them are often feasted on shortly after. Their complexion is like that of a rotting fish: pallid yellow skin with patches of green, slimy scales and bony protrusions. Their piscine eyes are similarly devoid of life with deep, black pupils surrounded by red that have dire effects on those they glare at.]

entries.name: Shadows
entries.content: [ Shadows are incorporeal and hard to see in dark areas but easy to see in brightly lit areas. Shadows hate life and light. Against living creatures, shadows are very aggressive and quick to attack, they are known to hesitate briefly when confronted with someone wearing a silkstone. Their favoured victims are innocent creatures, who lived morally good lives. The touch of a shadow is painfully chilly and saps the target's strength away.]

entries.name: Shambling Mound
entries.content: [ A shambling mound is a large, animated plant with predatory tendencies. It is also known as a shambler. They appear to be moving, vaguely man-shaped mounds of rotting vegetation. Shambling mounds feed off of the flesh and blood of living creatures they engulf and crush within their own bodies.]

entries.name: Shield Guardian
entries.content: [ A shield guardian is a powerful construct created to defend arcane spellcasters. They look something like a large stick figure made of wood with rocky appendages and metal parts. Each shield guardian is keyed to a special magical amulet. If the amulet is destroyed, the guardian will cease to function until keyed to a replacement amulet. A shield guardian protects its master with great speed and agility, attempting to deflect blows and attacks.]

entries.name: Shriekers
entries.content: [ Shriekers are human-sized mushrooms. They are similar in appearance to violet funghi, but lack the ability to move and do not have tentacles with which to poison prey. They can produce a loud, piercing, screaming sound that tends to attract curious creatures (or adventurers) to the area. They are immune to the poison of violet fungi. Shriekers can sense nearby motion or light and respond with a shriek. Each such screaming sound lasted between five and fifteen seconds.]

entries.name: Skeletons
entries.content: [ Skeletons are  undead animated corpses similar to zombies, but completely devoid of flesh and do not feed on the living. They can be made from virtually any solid creature, and as such their size and power varies widely. In addition to the basic humanoid skeleton, there are also skeletons created from wolves, trolls, ettins and even giants.]

entries.name: Solars
entries.content: [ Solars are the most powerful of all the angels and indeed of all the celestials. Described by some as truly godlike, only the celestial paragons are more glorious and powerful. Solars never take their own worshipers. Instead, they often serve as the direct hand of the divine being to whom they owe their allegiance to. Even the demon lords fear these holy celestial beings. Like planetars, solars can pray for and cast divine magical spells like the most powerful of clerics.]

entries.name: Specter
entries.content: [ A specter appears as a humanoid, with a mostly transparent and faintly luminous form. They look much as they did in life, though the injuries that cause their violent deaths are visible on many specimen and can be recognized by someone who knows what the person looked like. They are about the same size as a humanoid but weightless. A specter's touch isn't only painful; it also drains the life energy from living creatures.]

entries.name: Spirit Nagas
entries.content: [ Spirit nagas are the most powerful type of naga and akin to witches among other naga races. They have a human female head on a snake body, serpentine bodies with black scales, and red bands. Their humanoid faces are  framed with stringy hair. They are even more mysterious and enigmatic than the others of their kind, seeking lost magic to a fanatical extent. Spirit nagas are powerful spellcasters. The bite of a spirit naga is deadly, as it contains venom.]

entries.name: Sprites
entries.content: [ Sprites are the warrior relatives of pixies. They are fierce defenders of good wherever they dwell and also firm judges of other creatures' hearts and intentions. The term \"sprite\" actually has two meanings: the first meant the specific race of tiny warriors, while the second use referred to the group of tiny, insect-featured fey that the specific kind belongs to. Like other fey, sprites possess several innate magical powers: they can become invisible at will and detect good or evil.]

entries.name: Stirge
entries.content: [ A stirge is a tiny magical beast that feeds on the blood of other creatures. It resembles a monstrous cross between a large hummingbird and a mosquito. A group of stirges is known as a \"thirst\". Stirges are known to be used as familiars.]

entries.name: Stone Giants
entries.content: [ Stone giants, called steinjotunen in their own language, are a reclusive and artistic race of giants that live in underground and mountainous environments. The bodies of stone giants have a gray to grayish-brown skin tone, hair that ranges in a spectrum of dark grays and bluish-grays, and eyes of a silver or steel hue. Stone giants prefer to fight using ranged weapons such as boulders.]

entries.name: Stone Golems
entries.content: [ Stone golems are constructed from a single piece of carefully chiseled stone. The most elegant stone golems are used as both guardians and art pieces in a magical building. These constructs are generally made with a bipedal, humanoid shape, but stylized to suit their creator. Like any golem, these constructs possess an immunity to magic and cannot be harmed by normal weaponry.]

entries.name: Storm Giants
entries.content: [ Storm giants, known as uvarjotunen in their own language, are one of the most intelligent and respected races of giants. There are two ethnicities of storm giants; most have pale, light green skin and dark green hair and eyes, but a small number have violet skin, dark blue hair, and silver eyes. Storm giants have vision that is well adapted to underwater conditions, where they see equally as well as they did in the air. Storm giants innately have a high affinity for runecasting and  sorcery.]

entries.name: Succubus
entries.content: [ A succubus is a type of demon that exists to seduce and tempt mortals and ultimately slay them and take their life energy back to the Abyss. In her true form, a succubus appears as a stunningly beautiful woman of statuesque build and perfect figure, with flawless skin and red or raven-black hair, but also clawed fingers and large dark-hued or reddish bat-like wings mounted on their backs. With a kiss of her lips, an embrace, or something more intimate, a succubus drains the life of mortals.]

entries.name: Tarrasque
entries.content: [ The tarrasque is the most terrible creature known to inhabit the Prime Material Plane. The tarrasque is an enormous abomination, roughly the size of an ancient dragon, with two long horns extending from its forehead, a thick carapace, mighty tail, and a wide, toothy mouth. The tarrasque is impossible to frighten or charm and has resistances to every kind of damage imaginable. It has the ability to instill nearby creatures with terrible fear and ignore any natural resistances its victims have.]

entries.name: Treant
entries.content: [ A treant is a huge intelligent plant. Although a treant's wood appears to be solid like stone, it was filled with tubes that carry water from its roots to the areas where it is needed.]

entries.name: Troll
entries.content: [ Their deceptively thin bodies have thick, rubbery hides colored in shades of mossy green or putrid greys, and possess long hanging arms that end in massive claws. The skull of a troll has a messy, hair-like growth colored black or steel grey. Females are typically larger, and more powerful, than males.]

entries.name: Vampire
entries.content: [ Vampires are a type of undead that feed on blood. They are one of the most feared and powerful undead creatures. A vampire looks very much like it did when alive, but with paler skin, hardened and feral features giving them a predatory aspect, and red eyes that are hard to forget. They do not cast shadows and have no reflections in mirrors. A vampire retains all the abilities it had in life, and it gains the ability to drain blood and life energy, and to dominate others with its gaze.]

entries.name: Vampire Spawn
entries.content: [ Vampire spawn are undead created by vampires. A vampire spawn is innately subservient to the vampire that created it. They can only achieve free-will if their creator dies or if their creator voluntarily grants them freedom. Once free of their bondage a spawn cannot be enslaved again. They typically believe they are superior to other living or undead creatures, regardless of how powerful a creature actually is.]

entries.name: Violet Fungus
entries.content: [ A violet fungus is a type of subterranean fungus creature. Violet fungi can sense nearby motion and flail their appendages at creatures nearby. They feed on decaying matter, often from the bodies of creatures that came too close and had succumbed to their poison.]

entries.name: Vrock
entries.content: [ Vrocks, or type I demons, are tanar'ri with a taste for carnage and human flesh that appear to be humanoid vultures. Their bodies are twisted and gnarly with a long neck and limbs all covered in sinew. The parts of their body not covered in sinew, especially their broad wings, are coated with gray feathers. They are known among Abyssal denizens as untrustworthy and flighty creatures ruled by greed.]

entries.name: Water Elemental
entries.content: [ These elementals typically resemble a cresting wave of water. They can easily disappear within a body of water, becoming indistinguishable from all other liquids. Water elementals prefer to fight in bodies of water. They are capable of capsizing small boats and can impede the progress of larger craft. They will often attempt to grapple a larger creature or multiple smaller ones, restraining them within their watery body in an attempt to drown the victim(s).]

entries.name: Wight
entries.content: [ A wight is an undead creature given a semblance of life through sheer violence and hatred. They can drain the life energy of victims by touch, turning them into new wights upon death. Wights appear as weird and twisted reflections of the forms they had in life. They exist in a state between being alive and being dead.]

entries.name: Will-o'-Wisp
entries.content: [ The will-o'-wisp appears to be nothing more than a hazy ball of light, colored white, blue, violet, green, or yellow, glowing as brightly as a flaming torch. As such, it is easy to mistake one for a lantern, torch, or dancing lights. They tend to take on a blue, violet, or pale green hue whenever they are in combat. A will-o'-wisp avoids combat if at all possible, but will attack with electric shocks if pressed. It is immune to most spells.]

entries.name: Worg
entries.content: [ A worg is a type of magical beast that resembles a normal wolf but is larger, more intelligent, and has a fiendish countenance and glowing eyes. They will stalk humanoid prey for a number of hours or even days, choosing the best of time of day and terrain for the attack. Worgs were sometimes enslaved by orcs, goblins, and other such creatures to act as mounts or attack dogs. And sometimes they were specifically being bred for these purposes. They were also used as mounts by some bands of hobgoblins.]

entries.name: Wraith
entries.content: [ A wraith is an undead creature born of evil and darkness, despising light and all living things. They can drain the life from living creatures, turning them into new wraiths upon death. Wraiths are powerless in natural sunlight, appearing as a sinister, spectral figure robed in darkness. They have no visual features or appendages, except for their glowing red eyes.]

entries.name: Wyvern
entries.content: [ A wyvern is a large winged lizard, distantly related to the dragon, with a poisonous stinging tail and sharp teeth. Unlike true dragons, wyverns only have a pair of hind legs instead of a set four. Wyverns are aggressive and not greatly intelligent. When fighting these creatures dive down from above, grabbing prey with their hind leg claws, and then attempt to sting them to death.]

entries.name: Xorn
entries.content: [ Xorns are  very odd-looking creatures. They have radially symmetrical bodies with a large mouth at the top surrounded by three long arms interspersed with their three eyes. Their wide, pebbly, and rocky bodies rest upon three stumpy legs. They have talons at the end of their arms. Like many creatures from the Plane of Earth, xorns can travel through ground and stone as if it were water, leaving behind no tunnel at all. They always pass through the ground mouth-first.]

entries.name: Zombie
entries.content: [ A zombie is an undead creature usually created by the re-animation of a corpse. Unlike animated skeletons, zombies still retain some flesh on their bodies and gave off a horrid, rank smell. They are almost mindless, but can be given simple commands.]

entries.name: Athkatla
entries.content: [ Athkatla is the capital of the nation of Amn. It is a large port town that rests a few miles south of the Cloud Peaks, a prominent mountainous region. It is located in the middle of the trade route between southern provinces such as Calimshan, and northerly ones such as Waterdeep. Because of this, it is by far the largest and busiest harbour in all of Amn. Athkatla is led by a wealthy but corrupt government. The city is rife with crime and has a long standing fear of mages and sorcerers.]

entries.name: Amn
entries.content: [ Amn is a wealthy nation in western Faerûn. Prior to the Spellplague and the continent's disappearance, Amn held colonies far away in Maztica. Post-Spellplague it still controls important trade routes to Calimshan and Baldur's Gate as well as colonial ports in the Moonshaes and Chult. The crowning jewel of this powerful state is the capital city of Athkatla.]

entries.name: Faerûn
entries.content: [ The continent of Faerûn is a landmass located mainly in the northern hemisphere of the world of Toril. Besides the exterior coastline to the west and south, the most dominant feature on the continent is the Sea of Fallen Stars. Next in significance is the Shaar that separates the area around the inland sea from the coastal nations. To the east, Faerûn is bordered by a vast region of steppes, in the north are massive glaciers and tundra. South of the continent is the sub-tropical land of Zakhara.]

entries.name: Rauxes
entries.content: [ For 600 years, Rauxes stood as the capital of the Great Kingdom, bearing witness to both the empire’s greatest glories and its most savage depravity. In 586 CY, Rauxes’ long reign as imperial capital came to an end when Patriarch-General Pyrannden of Hextor announced that Ivid V was no longer overking. Within minutes, a ferocious magical battle broke out on the streets of the imperial city as rival princes desperately vied for the Malachite Throne. What happened next none can say.]

entries.name: the Great Kingdom
entries.content: [ The Great Kingdom, also known as Aerdy, is a kingdom in the World of Greyhawk]

entries.name: Maztica
entries.content: [ Maztica, referred to by its inhabitants as The True World, is a large continent west of Faerûn. Maztica is a land of jungles and mystery. North of Maztica is the continent of Anchorome and south of it is Lopango. Maztica was primarily inhabited by humans. These humans were split into four basic ethnic groups, the Payits , the Nexalans, the Green Folk, and the North Ones (more commonly called the Dog People).]

entries.name: Anchorome
entries.content: [ Sometimes referred to as the Anchorome Archipelago, it was a poorly known region composed of vast fertile lands and several islands. It constituted the northern portion of the large landmass in the planet's western hemisphere. Anchorome is a vast land with numerous islands. It is located along the northwestern shore of the Trackless Sea, west of Evermeet and north of Maztica. Northern Anchorome is described as an icy region. The southeastern regions of the continent are covered in jungle.]

entries.name: Lopango
entries.content: [ Lopango, also known as the Land of Fire, is a land on the southern end of Maztica. It is covered in forest or jungle and high mountains. Lopango was once part of Merrouroboros, the ancient super-continent that eventually broke up into Faerûn, Kara-Tur, Maztica, and Zakhara.]

entries.name: Merrouroboros
entries.content: [ Merrouroboros was a super-continent in existence on the planet Abeir-Toril during the Days of Thunder and before the Sundering of Abeir from Toril. Merrouroboros ceased to exist around −17,600 DR in the great cataclysm known as the First Sundering, which caused the super-continent to break apart into Faerûn, Maztica, and Katashaka, and the appearance of Evermeet.]

entries.name: Katashaka
entries.content: [ Katashaka is a continent a long distance to the southwest of Faerûn. In some outlandish old stories, it is called the "Dark Continent".]

entries.name: Trackless Sea
entries.content: [ The Trackless Sea is the name of the ocean due west of the continent of Faerûn. The Trackless Sea runs from the Sea of Swords in the west to Maztica, where it is known as Taylola or the Eastern Ocean, and to Anchorome in the east. The sea also spans north to the Sea of Moving Ice and south to the peninsula of Chult.]

entries.name: Evermeet
entries.content: [ The island nation Evermeet, occasionally known as the Green Isle, is the last true kingdom of, and the final destination for all non-drow Tel'Quessir ("elves") on Faerûn. Very few non-elves have ever been permitted to visit. Much of Evermeet's architecture was created by magical means, most notably by the use of the spell construction.]

entries.name: Sea of Moving Ice
entries.content: [ The Sea of Moving Ice, also referred to as the Floating Land by the Reghedmen barbarians, is a collection of icebergs and frost-covered isles that float in the waters of northwest Faerûn. The Sea of Moving Ice is located west of Icewind Dale and northwest of the Cold Run. Almost completely uncharted, the ice masses set wide enough apart for a ship to pass. The ice of the sea changed so that all but the most experienced seafarers could be caught off guard.]

entries.name: Reghedmen
entries.content: [ The Reghedmen, also known as the Reghed barbarians or the men of the tundra, are the barbarian tribes of Icewind Dale. The Reghedman were tall for humans, sometimes reaching seven feet in height. They were blue-eyed and fair-haired, with hair of blond, red, or light brown hues. The Reghedmen were migratory hunters, who herds of reindeer across the frozen tundra. They lived in deerskin tents and crafted goods of wood and whalebone.]

entries.name: Reghed Glacier
entries.content: [ The Reghed Glacier is a glacial wasteland north of the Spine of the World. The region is so desolate and isolated that few travelers dare to cross near its eastern border, let alone venture atop its icy facade. The Reghedman barbarians of Icewind Dale took their name from this glacier. In contrast to the unforgiving cold, Evermelt is a bubbling spring, a haven of warmth and a sacred location to the barbarian tribes.]

entries.name: Evermelt
entries.content: [ The Evermelt was a subterranean hot spring found within a cave at the base of the Reghed Glacier. It was considered a holy place by the Reghedmen barbarians of nearby Icewind Dale. The warm, tranquil waters of Evermelt appeared as a serene turquoise color that glittered like gold. Despite its mostly still waters, it had a small undercurrent that could pull one beneath the surface. This current leads to a small tunnel that opens up into the former lair of the white dragon Ingeloakastimizilian.]

entries.name: Ingeloakastimizilian
entries.content: [ Ingeloakastimizilian, also known as Icingdeath was a white dragon who lived in a region of the Reghed Glacier known as Evermelt. He spent most of his time sleeping on a bed of ice that covered his hoard. The barbarian tribes north of the Spine of the World mountains called him "Icingdeath".]

entries.name: Icewind Dale
entries.content: [ Icewind Dale is an arctic tundra located in the Frozenfar region of the North, known for being the northernmost explored region in all of Faerûn. It earned its name from the harsh winds and icy storms that destroyed buildings and scoured the landscape. The dale is a harsh, near-inhospitable land that regularly plunges below freezing temperatures, and receives little sunlight, particularly during the severe winter months.]

entries.name: Frozenfar
entries.content: [ The Frozenfar was the coldest, most remote region of the North. It comprised the Spine of the World mountains; the frigid lands to the north and west; including Icewind Dale, the Cold Run, the icebergs of the Sea of Moving Ice, and the northeasternmost part of the Trackless Sea.]

entries.name: Spine of the World
entries.content: [ The Spine of the World is a mountain range that stretched across the northwest region of Faerûn from the Cold Run near the Sea of Moving Ice, to the Ice Spires north of the Silver Marches. To many Faerûnians, the Spine of the World is simply an endless, nearly–impassable range of high, jagged, perpetually ice-covered mountains. While the western-most edge of the Spine is penetrated by a circuitous, always dangerous trade route to Icewind Dale, the rest was not even approached by most.]

entries.name: Cold Run
entries.content: [ The Cold Run was a large stretch of frigid tundra that runs from the mouth of the Iceflow to Icewind Dale. Long ago, part of the Cold Run was struck by either a heavy meteor strike or the lava of a volcanic eruption. This formed a huge crater, which was filled with rich ore.]

entries.name: Chult
entries.content: [ Chult is located at the westernmost end of the Chultan peninsula, in the southern part of the Trackless Sea, off the coast of Calimshan. Following the Second Sundering, it was reunited with the mainland. Regardless of geographical status, Chult has always been remote and isolated, forming a mountainous jungle of savage beasts, hulking dinosaurs, and disease-ridden swamps. Human tribes, goblins, and even stranger monstrous folk haunted the thick jungles.]

entries.name: Chultan Peninsula
entries.content: [ The Chultan Peninsula is the dominant area of Southwest Faerûn. It has an undeserved reputation of being a backward place with a complete lack of civilisation populated by savages. In fact, it boasts several large cities with stable governments that are all rife with culture.]

entries.name: Sea of Swords
entries.content: [ The Sea of Swords is a region of the Trackless Sea that separated the western coast of Faerûn (known as the Sword Coast) from the Nelanther Isles and the Moonshae Isles. At least one kingdom of sea elves, known as Nindrol, claimed the waters around the island of Toaridge-at-the-Sun's-Setting just north of the Nelanther (or the northernmost island of that group, according to some maps. It is not unusual for the Sea of Swords to be considered extending as far north as Luskan.]

entries.name: Nelanther
