entries.content: [ The Nelanther Isles, also just called the Nelanther, are a widely scattered chain of nearly one thousand islands west of Amn and Tethyr in the Trackless Sea. More than half the islands lack potable water and were an unfit place to live. The hundreds of islands that could support life were fought over by ruthless pirates. Among the islands, only the largest of the islands were named. Only a handful of these names were known to mainlanders, while the pirate captains knew them by heart.]

entries.name: Tethyr
entries.content: [ Tethyr is a nation in the Lands of Intrigue of west Faerûn. The Spires of Mir cover the southern highlands of Tethyr. Also known as the Wealdath, the Forest of Tethir is located along the Trade Way, south of the Small Teeth Mountains. In addition to the two elven tribes, Suldusk and Elmanesse, there are a variety of fey creatures that defended these woods as their home. A host of other dangers reside in these woods, including several dragons, wyverns, and even lycanthropes.]

entries.name: Lands of Intrigue
entries.content: [ Lands of Intrigue is a collective term used to describe Amn, Calimshan, Muranndin, Erlkazar, Velen and Tethyr. An older term for the same territory is the Empires of the Sands.]

entries.name: Muranndin
entries.content: [ The monster kingdom of Muranndin borders Amn in the north via the Small Teeth Mountains, Tethyr's northern Wealdath forest in the east, and west with the Dragon's Head peninsula. This left the independent duchy of Velen isolated from the rest of Faerûn. The monarch of this kingdom was called the Great Mur which usually was the chieftain of the strongest tribe. The Great Mur is responsible for essentially keeping the other tribes and bandits together and prevent infighting between them.]

entries.name: Erlkazar
entries.content: [ Erlkazar is a small kingdom located due east of Tethyr. The Snowflake Mountains are a range of very high mountains, some boasting a height in excess of 20,000 ft (6,100 m) above sea level. Impresk Lake is an icy cold lake fed by many sources. The Deepwash survived the drying up of Shalane lake. It is unknown if the ancient dragon turtle commonly known to live beneath the surface still resides in its waters. The Kuldin Peaks are home to the Starrock tribe of goblins that waged war on Erlkazar.]

entries.name: Snowflake Mountains
entries.content: [ The Snowflake Mountains are a range of mountains in West Faerûn, forming the borders between Tethyr, Amn, and what was once the barony of Impresk within Erlkazar. They include some of the tallest mountains in Faerûn.]

entries.name: Impresk
entries.content: [ Impresk is the barony responsible for ensuring that the monster population of the Snowflake Mountains remains low and defending the trade road to Riatavin. The barony is inhabited by many "hill clans" and contains several farming villages, a few logging and shepherding towns in the foothills, and a single mining town.]

entries.name: Riatavin
entries.content: [ Riatavin is a city in Tethyr in west Faerûn. Riatavin has a significant criminal underworld and the Shadow Thieves are the dominant criminal organization. The city also suffers from bandit incursions from Erlkazar.]

entries.name: Impresk Lake
entries.content: [ The Deepwash is a freshwater lake and, as of 1370–1372 DR, the largest lake in the Vilhon Reach. The northwestern stretch is known as Shalane Lake in Erlkazar. The lake is very deep and home to a very large dragon turtle, with a shell 30 feet (10 meters) in diameter, who resided near the lizardfolk city of Surkh. In Surkh, the dragon turtle was highly respected, and some even worshiped it, believing it to be an honor to be killed and eaten by it. The turtle was large enough to capsize ships.]

entries.name: Deepwash
entries.content: [ The Deepwash is a freshwater lake and, as of 1370–1372 DR, the largest lake in the Vilhon Reach. The northwestern stretch is known as Shalane Lake in Erlkazar. The lake is very deep and home to a very large dragon turtle, with a shell 30 feet (10 meters) in diameter, who resided near the lizardfolk city of Surkh. In Surkh, the dragon turtle was highly respected, and some even worshiped it, believing it to be an honor to be killed and eaten by it. The turtle was large enough to capsize ships.]

entries.name: Lake of Steam
entries.content: [ The Lake of Steam, also known as Arnaden, is a region in south Faerûn. Despite its name, the Lake of Steam is in fact an inland sea connected to the Shining Sea. On its shores was a collection of free cities, mainly on the northern and western sides. The southern side, by contrast, was a collection of kingdoms collectively named the Border Kingdoms.]

entries.name: Border Kingdoms
entries.content: [ The Border Kingdoms occupy an area of lush grasslands between the Lake of Steam and the Shaar. This area is divided politically into many smaller principalities and kingdoms. Because of the instability of the Border Kingdoms, no accurate maps exist and the borders move around as rulers and boundaries change — this is the ideal place for adventurers wanting to start a kingdom of their own. A borderer is the name given to an inhabitant of the Border Kingdoms.]

entries.name: Shaar
entries.content: [ The Shaar is a vast land of plains in south Faerûn. The lands to the west of the Landrise aregenerally called the Shaar, while those to the east are the Eastern Shaar. By 1479 DR, due to the Spellplague of 1385 DR, the Shaar had become a vast desert wasteland known as the Shaar Desolation. In the center of the Shaar Desolation lays an enormous area called the Underchasm where huge swathes of land around the Great Rift collapsed into the Underdark.]

entries.name: Eastern Shaar
entries.content: [ The Eastern Shaar is the eastern extension of the Shaar. Its major feature are the Council Hills.]

entries.name: Council Hills
entries.content: [ The Council Hills are a clump of hills in the Eastern Shaar where the territories of several Shaaran tribes meet. The hills were home to the long-destroyed city of Shandaular and have since been mere ruins. Beneath the hills are remains of the old city, a series of underground tunnels.]

entries.name: Underchasm
entries.content: [ The Underchasm is a huge canyon created by the spellplague in 1385 DR that runs roughly north to south from Akanûl to the borders of Halruaa. The chasm extends all the way to the Underdark. The upper Underchasm is home to many flying monsters such as dragons.]

entries.name: Underdark
entries.content: [ The Underdark is the vast network of underground caverns and tunnels underneath the surface of Abeir-Toril. It is home to a host of evil beings driven deep into the caverns at the end of the age of demons. The Underdark was not one giant cavern under Faerûn, but rather, many huge networks of caverns and caves. The major domains of the Underdark were the Buried Realms, the Darklands, the Deep Wastes, the Earthroot, the Glimmersea, Great Bhaerynden, the Northdark, and Old Shanatar.]

entries.name: Abeir-Toril
entries.content: [ Abeir-Toril is the name of a prehistoric planet that existed before −31,000 DR when Ao sundered the world into two worlds: Abeir and Toril. The name is archaic, meaning "cradle of life".]

entries.name: Abeir
entries.content: [ Abeir was the twin planet of Toril, located in the same material plane of its sibling world, but within a "pocket dimension" that was out of synchrony with Toril.]

entries.name: Toril
entries.content: [ Toril was the third planet from the Sun in Realmspace. It was orbited by one moon named Selûne, and by a cluster of asteroids, known as the Tears of Selûne.]

entries.name: Buried Realms
entries.content: [ The whole of the Buried Realms was bordered by the Sharnwall. This magical artifice was created in ancient times by the sharn to imprison the phaerimm. It functioned as a barrier, confining the phaerimm to the Buried Realms. They could not travel between their realm and the rest of Faerûn by any skill or magic they were capable of. However, all other creatures could cross it freely.]

entries.name: Sharn Wall
entries.content: [ The Sharn Wall, also seen as Sharnwall, was a shimmering, silver-colored magical barrier in Anauroch created by the sharn to imprison the phaerimm.]

entries.name: Darklands
entries.content: [ The Darklands are located underneath the heart of Faerûn and formed an important domain of the Underdark. Located above the Darklands is the Dragon Coast, portions of the Orsraun Mountains, Turmish, and Chessenta. This vast subterranean realm stretches all the way from Cairnheim in the west to Traaskl Thorog in the east.]

entries.name: Dragon Coast
entries.content: [ The Dragon Coast region is located on the southern shore of the Dragonmere, and at the western extent of the Sea of Fallen Stars.]

entries.name: Dragonmere
entries.content: [ The Dragonmere (also known as the Lake of Dragons) is a lake on the Dragon Coast at the western edge of the Sea of Fallen Stars. Cormyr and Sembia are on the northern part of this lake, with the Dragon Coast along the south. The Dragonmere was almost 100 miles from north to south at its widest point. As of 1372 DR, at its narrowest point it is ten miles wide, with Westgate to the south, and Urmlaspyr to the north.]

entries.name: Orsraun Mountains
entries.content: [ The Orsraun Mountains are the largest range of mountains south of the Spine of the World.]

entries.name: Turmish
entries.content: [ Turmish is a republic with the capital of Alaghôn, and was located in the north of the Vilhon Reach. It is a densely populated nation, with bustling cities that are home to many mercenary companies and mercantile organizations that trade across all of Faerûn. As the saying from Starmantle goes: "The hordes of Turmish are as numerous as the waves upon the Inner Sea".]

entries.name: Vilhon Reach
entries.content: [ Through its many port cities, the Vilhon Reach is established as an essential trade center between the cities of the southern bodies of water, the Lake of Steam, the Shining Sea, and the many kingdoms and city-states around the inner sea of the continent, the Sea of Fallen Stars.]

entries.name: Alaghôn
entries.content: [ Alaghôn, the capital of Turmish, is an ancient city that saw its share of trials and tribulations over the years, ranging from terrible fires to occupation by the blue dragon Anaglathos during the Reign of the Wyrm. Throughout all of this, Alaghôn survived as a trade center known as the "throne of Turmish.]

entries.name: Starmantle
entries.content: [ Starmantle is a small city located on the Dragon Coast. It was one of Westgate's main rivals for trade across the Sea of Fallen Stars.]

entries.name: Westgate
entries.content: [ Westgate is a seedy and squalid metropolis—with a history in piracy, powerful crime syndicates, and nameless vampiric crime-lords. Westgate thrived on black-market trade and corruption, and was perhaps one of the most sordid cities in all of Faerûn. The legacy of scoundrels and spies is found in every alley, and danger lurks for the unprepared in every corner. It is probably the oldest, richest and most corrupt port on the Sea of Fallen Stars. ]

entries.name: Sea of Fallen Stars
entries.content: [ The Sea of Fallen Stars, also known as the Inner Sea, was the largest inland body of water in Faerûn.]

entries.name: Chessenta
entries.content: [ Chessenta is a confederation of city-states bound by common culture and mutual defense, but for most of its history wasn’t truly a unified nation and the Chessentan cities were often at war with one another. Chessenta is one of the so-called Old Empires of Faerûn.]

entries.name: Old Empires
entries.content: [ The Old Empires (also called the Old Kingdoms) was the collective term used by most people to describe the empires of Chessenta, Mulhorand, and Unther, due to their origins being traced back to thousands of years before the Time of Troubles.]

entries.name: Mulhorand
entries.content: [ Mulhorand was one of the Old Empires in eastern Faerûn. Mulhorand was destroyed by the Spellplague and the empire of High Imaskar came to comprise its former territories. After the Chosen of the Mulhorandi gods appeared around the time of the Second Sundering, however, they and the wizard Nezram rallied the Mulan to overthrow the Imaskari once more, driving them into the Plains of Purple Dust.]

entries.name: High Imaskar
entries.content: [ High Imaskar was an empire that stood on the shattered ruins of Mulhorand on the eastern shore of the Sea of Fallen Stars, after the Spellplague of 1385 DR. It represented one of two nations of Imaskari survivors in the 15th century DR, until its eventual destruction in 1487 DR, during the final events of the Second Sundering.]

entries.name: Plains of Purple Dust
entries.content: [ The Plains of Purple Dust was a vast windy desert located east of the Dragonsword Mountains on the edge of the region occupied by Mulhorand. The Plains of Purple Dust was covered with a purple-colored dust that radiated faint magic and stony crags and rocky badlands.]

entries.name: Dragonsword Mountains
entries.content: [ The Dragonsword Mountains, located in central Mulhorand, served as a barrier between the Plains of Purple Dust and the rest of the nation.]

entries.name: Unther
entries.content: [ Unther was one of the Old Empires in east Faerûn. The Untherans were brought to Toril from Earth by the Imaskar Empire looking for some manpower. With the help of their deities, the former slaves freed themselves and settled the lands that later became Unther.]

entries.name: Nedeheim
entries.content: [ Nedeheim (meaning "Down-home" in the Giant language) was an ancient kingdom of stone giants north of Shanatar. It fell to dwarves during the Giant Wars.]

entries.name: Deep Wastes
entries.content: [ The Deep Wastes formed a small domain part of the vast Underdark hidden away underneath the surface of the Dalelands and the Moonsea. The region was sparsely populated due to the collapse of the drow city of Maerimydra which once held Shadowdale as a conquered surface land.]

entries.name: Dalelands
entries.content: [ The Dalelands was a region in north Faerûn of dense forests and bountiful, rolling farmlands.]

entries.name: Moonsea
entries.content: [ The Moonsea was a region in north Faerûn, dominated by the large titular sea that was connected to the Sea of Fallen Stars to the south by the River Lis.]

entries.name: Earthroot
entries.content: [ The Earthroot was a vast domain in the Underdark. Since it lay beneath the Unapproachable East few people knew of its existence and even fewer explorers mapped its tunnels and caves. The most mysterious and greatest hidden realm in the Earthroot was the realm of Deep Imaskar itself. It lay below the Endless Wastes in the most eastern part of the Earthroot.]

entries.name: Unapproachable East
entries.content: [ Deep Imaskar, also known as The City of the Great Seal, was created during the fall of the Imaskar Empire in −2481 DR by the wizard lord Ilphemon as a safe haven for his followers and family. They fled carrying an artifact of immense power.]

entries.name: Hordelands
entries.content: [ The Hordelands, also known as The Endless Wastes and as Taan by the natives, was once part of the territory of the mighty empire of Imaskar and was populated by horsemen tribes, most notably the Tuigans.]

entries.name: Glimmersea
entries.content: [ The Glimmersea, sometimes called the Sea of the Starry Night, was a vast underground ocean lying in the Underdark of Toril. The Glimmersea consisted of a large body of water filling dozens of huge vaults, some thousands of feet (hundreds of meters) high. It was famous for the many ribbon cascades of water that sprayed down from the high ceilings. Its name, "Sea of the Starry Night", was derived from the luminescent rocks found in the ceilings of some of the vaults of the Glimmersea.]

entries.name: Great Bhaerynden
entries.content: [ Great Bhaerynden was a domain located in the south-central region of Faerûn beneath the vast plains of Shaar. This Underdark region was the first homeland of the dwarves, but was conquered by the drow when they first ventured in the Underdark in search of a realm of their own. Gold dwarves live in the Great Rift and a lot of the adjoining caves. Drow and half-drow held the city of T'lindhet, and halflings lived in Deepburrow in Great Bhaerynden.]

entries.name: Northdark
entries.content: [ The Northdark was an underground domain of the Underdark north and east of the city of Waterdeep. The area was home to some of the most renowned subterranean realms of Faerûn like the svirfneblin ruins of Blingdenstone, the duergar deepkingdom of Gracklstugh and the drow cities of Menzoberranzan and Ched Nasad.]

entries.name: Blingdenstone
entries.content: [ At the entrance to the city of Blingdenstone was a set of stairs and a large iron gate. Just past the gate, inside the city, was a large and winding maze aimed to slow down any would-be invaders. The city itself consisted of many cavern chambers connected by winding tunnels. The city's appearance was organic, carved smoothly into the stone. Many buildings appeared as simple piles of rocks but were in fact masterfully carved to appear so.]

entries.name: Gracklstugh
entries.content: [ Gracklstugh was a cavern city and subterranean port. It had smelters and foundries mingling among stalagmites. The air smelled acrid and was filled with industrial sounds: fire, steam, and iron ringing. The city was lit by firelight. The cavern sloped down on the eastern side to join the Darklake. The city was mainly home to duergar, but there was a sizable minority of derro who lived there, as well as a number of durzagon, orogs, and stone giants.]

entries.name: Ched Nasad
entries.content: [ The city was located in a large V-shaped cavern. The grotto was nearly a mile high and half a mile wide at the top (narrower at the bottom). The walls of the cavern were very steep. The city had magically controlled lighting. The city structure was built of layers of petrified webs that were bathed in faerie fire that was usually purple, amber, green, and yellow. Hundreds of webs stretch across the cavern, with nearly vertical webs connecting layers.]

entries.name: Old Shanatar
entries.content: [ Compared to the other major Underdark domains, Old Shanatar had the most non-natural tunnels, passages, and halls, though were some were of amazingly huge scale. Just like the Northdark, inhabitants and adventurers alike had fairly well explored and mapped the passages of Old Shanatar.]

entries.name: Shining Sea
entries.content: [ The Shining Sea was one of the great seas of Faerûn. The sea stretched from the coastline of Chult in the south, to the shoreline of Calimshan in the north. The Shining Sea had a large amount of trade and traffic. It was quite large, although it was not as large as the Trackless Sea or the Sea of Swords.]

entries.name: Kuldin Peaks
entries.content: [ The Kuldin Peaks were a small cluster of mountains in the country of Erlkazar at the border with Tethyr.]

entries.name: Velen
entries.content: [ Velen was nestled between two ocean-side hills, Captain's Cliff on the west and Widow's Hill to the east.[3] The city was guarded by massive, copper-colored stone walls that protected both its coast and overland borders. It's wharf was equipped with massive chains, submerged beneath the sea, that could be hoisted to hem the speed and maneuverability of any ships that tried to bombard the city. The Velean were a hearty and resourceful people.]

entries.name: Spires of Mir
entries.content: [ The Spires of Mir were a wasteland of strange stone spires located in southern Tethyr. Prior to the Spellplague, the spires were part of the Forest of Mir, but the plague changed the trees into huge stone spires. Not only was the landscape warped by the Spellplague, but so too were the creatures that roamed the land, which were transformed into dangerous beasts.]

entries.name: Forest of Tethir
entries.content: [ The Forest of Tethir, also known as Wealdath was the largest forest in the Lands of Intrigue and on the Sword Coast and one of the largest in all of Faerûn. Some scholars were of the opinion that the forest was the "single most important thing" that set the culture of Tethyr.]

entries.name: Trade Way
entries.content: [ The Trade Way started at Calimport in the south and traveled along the coast line all the way north to Waterdeep. The section of road between Baldur's Gate and Tethyr was also known as the Coast Way on some maps.]

entries.name: Calimport
entries.content: [ Calimport was the sprawling capital city of the country of Calimshan. For most of its existence, it was by far the largest city in all of Faerûn. Because Calimport had such a long history, including at least twelve times the city had been almost completely destroyed by fire or other calamity, most of the older buildings of the city had been rebuilt or merged into newer ones. One could find ancient byways, rooms, or other structures integrated into others.]

entries.name: Coast Way
entries.content: [ The Coast Way was a long, well-traveled trade road along the west coast of Faerûn. The Coast Way was just a part of the much larger Trade Way that started at Calimport in the south and went along the coastline all the way north to Waterdeep. The section of road between Baldur's Gate and Tethyr was generally known as the Coast Way.]

entries.name: Calimshan
entries.content: [ Calimshan was a nation which covered the southern corner of West Faerûn, including the Calim Desert and the Spider Swamp. From the deserts to western shores to the swamps in the east and plains in between, Calimshan provided for a range of environments. As with the rest of Faerûn, this was a heavily human country. The history of the Calishites led them to have deeply rooted ties to the Genies that long since have left the lands.]

entries.name: Calim Desert
entries.content: [ The Calim Desert, also known as the Skyfire Wastes,[3] was a rocky desert on the coast in the country of Calimshan. It was not formed by natural means, instead being the result of an epic magical war between two genies, the djinni Calim and efreeti Memnon. The sands hid the ruins of ancient cities, which were said to hold many treasures.]

entries.name: Spider Swamp
entries.content: [ The Spider Swamp was a hot, fetid swamp resting at the southwestern corner of Calimshan.]

entries.name: Moonshae Isles
entries.content: [ The Moonshae Isles were a group of islands that formed a roughly circular archipelago with the Sea of Moonshae in the center. The Moonshae Isles were populated mainly by the Ffolk and the Northlanders, two human societies. Over the one hundred years since Queen Alicia consolidated her rule, the two groups intermarried and became more culturally unified.]

entries.name: Nindrol
entries.content: [ Nindrol was an undersea kingdom of sea elves that occupied the waters around the island of Toaridge-at-the-Sun's-Setting in the Sea of Swords circa the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR. The kingdom contained forests, labyrinths, and warrens of coral. Some "stacks" rivaled the tallest towers and turrets of any castle on the mainland. The Nindrollen were relatively carefree and enjoyed teasing any merchant vessels or pirate ships that sailed over their territory.]

entries.name: Baldur's Gate
entries.content: [ Baldur's Gate, was the largest metropolis and city-state on the Sword Coast, within the greater Western Heartlands. It was a crowded city of commerce and opportunity. The strong peace-keeping force known as the Watch, along with the presence of the powerful Flaming Fists mercenary company, kept the city generally peaceful and safe. Baldurians took great pride in the inclusiveness of their city. Since its famous tax revolt, Baldur's Gate was ruled by four Grand Dukes.]

entries.name: City of Brass
entries.content: [ The City of Brass is built upon a forty-mile diameter glowing brass hemisphere that floats above rivers of magma and the fiery lakes and seas of the plane. At the Grand Sultan's command, the hemisphere can sink into a sea of flame so that the ports can be used. The rulers and most common race in the City of Brass are the efreet, though other races - including humanoid ones like humans, elves, etc. - are allowed to dwell within the city's walls as well.]

entries.name: Hykanask
entries.content: [ Hykanask is a gnoll spire-city located on Vorganund, the 52nd layer of the Abyss.]

entries.name: Vorganund
entries.content: [ Vorganund is the 52nd layer of the Abyss.]

entries.name: Abyss
entries.content: [ The Abyss, also known as The Infinite Layers of the Abyss, or Demonholme, is one of the planes of existence. It is best known as the home of demons, including the numerous varieties of tanar'ri. The Abyss is unique in that it is divided into an uncountable number of independent planes. Each has its own unique and terrible terrain. Controlling at least one level of the Abyss usually qualifies a demon to claim the rank of demon lord.]

entries.name: Kretor
entries.content: [ Kretor is a militant city-state controlled by devils. 90% of the population of Kretor are lawful evil in alignment. The population includes cultists who worship devils, and those who have sold their souls for power. The city is divided into six sectors, each ruled by a horned devil loyal to the city's ruler. In turn, each horned devil has a number of lieutenants, who work with human worshipers and ensure that other devils do not muscle in their master's territory.]

entries.name: Ravens Bluff
entries.content: [ The city of Ravens Bluff attracted the ambitious and adventurous folks of Faerûn, particularly during the economic boom of the 1370s DR. It was considered the "place to be" for those looking to find their fortune in the northern Sea of Fallen Stars. Its people were a hard-working, active lot who, failing an education, were at least skilled in their trade or experienced in their line of work.]

entries.name: Silverymoon
entries.content: [ Silverymoon is often dubbed the “Gem of the North,” for it resembles and emulates the lost elven city of Myth Drannor in many respects. It is one of the few civilized places in the middle of the rough and untamed wilderness that is the North of Faerûn. It has a rich cultural life and is renowned as a meeting place for all races that are morally inclined towards good.]

entries.name: Myth Drannor
entries.content: [ Myth Drannor, formerly known as Cormanthor the City of Song, was once considered to be the most beautiful and peaceful of any of the cities in Faerûn. At its peak, no city could compare to the glory of Myth Drannor. All races lived in complete harmony for the first time in memory, without fear or corruption. However, the city has been in ruins for many years. The city was once protected by a device called a mythal which is one of the greatest spells in perhaps all of the Realms.]

entries.name: mythal
entries.content: [ The mythal is a protective spell which shields Myth Drannor from outside forces and from general harm.]

entries.name: Sterngate
entries.content: [ Sterngate is a city best known for the Siege of Sterngate, in which the city was attacked by boulder-throwing giants.]

entries.name: Tiera Minuut
entries.content:
[ Tiera Minuut is one of the few interplanar cities on the Elemental Plane of Ice .

Tiera Minuut is a great flying castle once watched over by a goddess of wind. Now, abandoned by the forgotten deity, it drifts over the Plane of Ice, a bastion of comparative warmth. It's still quite cold, but, by mortal standards, quite a bit less life-threatening than the rest of the plane. The city is ruled by a Council of Nine, and has an open door policy, accepting all who would seek shelter from the cold.]

entries.name: Plane of Ice
entries.content: [ This elemental plane is a plane of endless ice and cold, home to the coldest places in the multiverse.]

entries.name: Vorkehan, City of Fumes
entries.content: [ The City of Fumes is the planar headquarters of the Mercykiller faction, a place where punishment is seen as a virtue, a necessary step in reforming those who seek to violate the law...and all seek to violate the law at some point. Justice is harsh, terrifying, and swift here, and all of the residents are eager to dispense it. A magical tower that overlooks the city, called the Eye of Rigelus, records every action of every person in the city, ensuring that all illegal activities are documented.]

entries.name: Zakhara
entries.content: [ Zakhara, also known as the Land of Fate, is a giant peninsula of the same super-continent that hosts Faerûn and Kara-Tur on the planet Abeir-Toril. The Land of Fate was home to a diversity of non-human inhabitants, but the majority comprised human Zakharans with brown skin, dark hair, and relatively small height. The seas around Zakhara were plagued with pirates and corsairs. The land was full of secretive cities, unwelcoming to travelers, huge deserts, lush oases and powerful genies.]

entries.name: Kara-Tur
entries.content: [ Kara-Tur is a continent lying east of Faerûn on Toril. Between Kara-Tur and Faerûn stretches the Hordelands for hundreds of miles. The various countries of Kara-Tur include the following: Shou Lung, T'u Lung, Tabot, the Plain of Horses, the Northern Wastes, Malatra, and the Island Kingdoms.]

entries.name: Shou Lung
entries.content: [ Shou Lung is arguably the most powerful nation on Toril. Places of interest include the port of Karatin, capital of the Hai Yuan, or Maritime provinces, and the Kao Shan province with the semi-independent city of Kai Shan. The main criminal organization in the country is the Tsui Tong.]

entries.name: Karatin
entries.content: [ Karatin was a seaport city at the mouth of the Hungtse River. It was built on a swamp, but partly settled on a cleared-out jungle. Karatin also had the Temple of the Jade Empress, a beautiful temple erected by the Sea Lords around a statue of the Empress Ti Hai Chin, wife of the Hai Dynasty's founder.]

entries.name: Hungtse
entries.content: [ The Hungtse River is one of the largest rivers on Toril, spanning over a thousand miles across both the Hordelands and Kara-Tur.]

entries.name: Kao Shan
entries.content: [ Kao Shan Province was a province of the empire of Shou Lung in Kara-Tur by the 14th century DR. It was also called the Province of the Mountains. In ancient times, it was a province of Anok-Imaskar and later an independent realm in its own right, called simply Kao Shan.]

entries.name: Tsui Tong
entries.content: [ The Tsui Tong was the primary criminal organization of the province of Kao Shan in the Shou Lung empire. It was based out of the city of Kai Shan and had become a political force in the area.]

entries.name: Great Sea
entries.content: [ The Great Sea, known as Bahr al-Kibar in Zakhara, is one of the larger seas of Toril, lying between the continents of Faerûn and Zakhara. The Great Sea is heated by strong warming ocean currents. These kept it noticeably warm south of Halruaa and in the eastern end. Beneath the waves dwell sea elves of a distinct ethnic type, having deep-green skin coloration and irregular brown patches and stripes. There are a large number of pirates and corsairs that operated out of the Great Sea.]

entries.name: Laerakond
entries.content: [ Laerakond is a large, horseshoe-shaped landmass, west of the Trackless Sea and north of the Great Sea. Like Faerûn, Laerakond also has its own Underdark region. However, this region is usually unknown even to the inhabitants. The continent is composed of mountain ranges on three sides, surrounding the great bay of the Dragon Sea. The entire continent is covered by arambar, causing the sky to be silver-colored. This phenomenon is called the Steelsky.]

entries.name: Dragon Sea
entries.content: [ The Dragon Sea was the largest inland body of water in Laerakond. The sea stretched from the coastline of Relmaur all the way south to the Great Sea. Its major areas included the bays of Relmaur to the north, Melabrauth and the Dusk Ports to the west, and Skelkor, Eskorn, the Sword Lands, and the Windrise Ports to the east.]

entries.name: Relmaur
entries.content: [ Relmaur is located in the southern, warmer slopes of the Howling Mountains range, and thus was composed by mountains covered by thick conifer forests, as well as high valleys, cliffs, rugged ravines, and waterfalls. Relmaur is ruled by the High Crown, a title always given to a dragonborn member of Clan Urlingscar, the ruling dragonborn clan since the creation of the kingdom. Relmaur is one of the few places where dragonborn could live free.]

entries.name: Melabrauth
entries.content: [ Melabrauth, also known as the Jungle Empire, is the oldest dragon empire of Laerakond. Melabrauth is ruled by Melauthaur the Undying One, a powerful dracolich. There are no known settlements or roads in Melabrauth. Its many rivers are navigable but infested by fierce and dangerous monsters. The only known inhabitants of Melabrauth are dragons and their dragonspawn servants. A few humans and dragonborn are allowed to live in Melabrauth, but only to serve as amusement for its dragon inhabitants.]

entries.name: Dusk Ports
entries.content: [ The Dusk Ports are a collection of seemingly free trade cities on the western shores of the Dragon Sea. In reality, they are vassal states to the green dragon Orlarrakh.]

entries.name: Skelkor
entries.content: [ Skelkor is the most powerful dragon empire of Laerakond as of 1479 DR. Many people consider it to be the evil empire of the continent. Skelkor is a land dominated by dragons. However, slaves of many humanoid races, mainly dragonborn, humans, halflings and a minority of genasi, compose the bulk of empire's population. Skelkor is ruled by Gauwervyndhal the Empress Dragon, one of the most powerful and feared dragons of Laerakond. She is served by her "suzerains", dragons directly related to her.]

entries.name: Sword Lands
entries.content: [ The Sword Lands are a prosperous land, with plenty trade, farming, hunting and freedom for all its inhabitants. No dragon dares to attack the Sword Lands, and many sages and wizards dedicate all of their lives to learn why. The reality of the situation are the fabled dragonheirs, humans with the ability to control dragons by gaze or touch, who probably still frightened the dragons, despite the fact that these near-mythical figures probably all died out in the past.]

entries.name: Windrise Ports
entries.content: [ The Windrise Ports were a loose confederation of independent, free port cities on the southeastern shores of the Dragon Sea. Those ports served as bastions of trade and civilization in Laerakond. Each port was an independent and self-ruling state, rival to each other but able to cooperate when was needed.]

entries.name: Bahamut
entries.content: [ Bahamut is the dragon god of justice. In his natural form, Bahamut is a massive dragon with a tail the same length as his body, with platinum scales tougher than any shield that glows with a faint blue sheen, and blue eyes, the exact color of which may have depended on Bahamut's mood. Wandering the mortal world, he usually takes the appearance of an old human or demihuman in peasant robes accompanied by seven canaries. His favored food is early morning frost on grass, honey, and daisy petals.]

entries.name: Tyr
entries.content: [ Tyr is the greater god of law and justice in the Faerûnian pantheon. He is the leader of the coalition of deities known as the Triad. Tyr was portrayed as blind or with a bloody bandage over his eyes and missing his right hand, for which he bore his title of the Maimed God. He is often shown wielding a powerful magic sword or warhammer and dressed in light armor or chainmail. He does not try to hide or bandage his stump.]

entries.name: Torm
entries.content: [ Torm known as The True and The Loyal Fury, is the god whose portfolio consisted of duty, loyalty, righteousness. Torm's divine realm is called Trueheart. In the Great Wheel cosmology, it is located in Mercuria, the second of the Seven Heavens. The origins of Torm were a mystery, although it is known he was once a mortal hero during the time of the fall of Netheril, who eventually became a demigod. Torm greatly reveres Tyr, seeing him as his spiritual father. He is also a staunch ally of Ilmater.]

entries.name: Ilmater
entries.content: [ Ilmater is the god of those who suffer, the oppressed, and the persecuted, who offers them relief and support, encourages them to endure and others to help them, to take their burdens or take their places. In avatar form, Ilmater appears as a short man with a burly build and wearing only a breechcloth, with a plain but kind and comforting face, balding head, and a hairy body. But this body bears the marks of mutilation and torture on the rack.]

entries.name: Moradin
entries.content: [ Moradin is the lawful good god of the dwarves and the chief deity in their pantheon. A harsh but fair judge, he is strength and force of will embodied. Moradin inspires dwarven inventions and constantly seeks to improve that race, encouraging their good nature, intelligence, and harmonious existence with other good races while battling their pride and isolationist tendencies.]

entries.name: Amaunator
entries.content: [ Amaunator is the Netherese solar deity of order, the sun, law, and time. He is viewed as a harsh but fair deity,revered by many rulers, soldiers, and powerful wizards in ancient Netheril. Amaunator's avatar, whose skin shed golden light, looked like a lanky, silver-white haired, and short man with a white tenday growth of beard clad in a long, flowing, black or purple gown with silver or gold trims, the uniform of a magistrate. Amaunator was viewed as a stern and unforgiving deity.]

entries.name: Berronar
entries.content: [ Berronar Truesilver is an intermediate deity in the dwarven pantheon. She is also known as The Revered Mother or the Mother of Safety. Berronar's clerics were known as faenor, which translated as "those of the home". Faenor served as the guardians and protectors of dwarven clans. They archived the lore, traditions, and family histories of the dwarves. By acting as teachers and healers, they aimed to further the good health and good character of the dwarven race.]

entries.name: Yondalla
entries.content: [ Yondalla is the creator of the halfling race and matriarch of not only the halfling pantheon, but the whole race itself. With her charming personality and friendly demeanor she was an example to all halflings; who almost all shared her curiosity, loyalty and sense of mischief. Powerful clerics of Yondalla were granted the ability to cast Curse of Yondalla, a spell reserved to be used against those who committed foul crimes against halflings.]

entries.name: Raven Queen
entries.content: [ The Raven Queen is a mysterious entity from the Shadowfell who is revered as a deity by the shadar-kai. The Raven Queen does not possess or manifest a physical form, instead appearing as a miscellany of symbols, perceptions, and images. One of the Raven Queen's divine realms in the Shadowfell is a castle known as the Fortress of Memories. It is a place of overwhelming sorrow, overflowing with memories taken from mortals and fragments of dead deities.]

entries.name: Helm
entries.content: [ Helm, also known as the Vigilant One and The Watcher, is the god of guardians, protection, and protectors. He is worshiped by guards and paladins both, long being seen as a cold and focused deity who impartially takes the role of defender and sometimes also enforcer. A very old deity, Helm is the eternal sentry and is always seen wearing a full suit of armor that represents the weight of his heavy responsibility. Helm was particularly fond of children, and often forgave minor transgressions.]

entries.name: Kelemvor
entries.content: [ Kelemvor, also known as the Lord of the Dead and Judge of the Damned, is the god of death and the dead, and master of the Crystal Spire in the Fugue Plane. Kelemvor promotes that death is a natural part of life and should not be feared as long as it is understood. As a result of his deep respect for life and death, he holds the undead in the uttermost contempt.]

entries.name: Mystra
entries.content: [ Mystra, the Mother of all Magic, is a greater deity. As a goddess, she could shape change at will and mortals who saw her reported she changed constantly. Mystra tends to the Weave constantly, making possible all the miracles and mysteries wrought by magic and users of magic. Mystra was said to be a manifestation of the Cosmic Balance—maintaining order in the world of magic by correcting great inequalities if things went askew.]

entries.name: Jergal
entries.content: [ Jergal, also referred to as The Lord of the End of Everything, is the seneschal of Kelemvor, and keeps records on the final disposition of all the spirits of the dead. Jergal is unfeeling and excessively formal, he never angers and always speaks in a disembodied, chilling voice. He cares little for anything besides an orderly accounting of the fate of the world as it slowly sinks into death.]

entries.name: Azuth
entries.content: [ Azuth is a Faerûnian god of of arcane magic whose concerns included the perpetuation of the magical arts as a craft. The lesser god is a servant of Mystra and worshiped by all manner of arcane spellcasters, earning particular veneration from wizards. The Lord of Spells often appeared as an elderly man with a long, white beard garbed in antique clothes and wielding a gem-topped staff.]

entries.name: Hoar
entries.content: [ Hoar, also known as The Doombringer, is the vengeful deity of retribution invoked by those who seeks to repay an eye for an eye. He is also an exarch of Bane. He is a bitter deity, prone to mood swings and fits of violence.]

entries.name: Null
entries.content: [ Null is the dragon god of death and undeath with two aspects, The Reaver and the Guardian of the Lost. As the Reaver, he is worshiped by evil dragons and takes lives, blessing those who served him in this capacity. As the Guardian, he ferries the souls of dead dragons to Dragon Eyrie and ensures they are no longer troubled by the enemies they may have had in life. Whichever role he was in at the time, he appeared as an impenetrable region of blackness in the shape of a dragon.]

entries.name: Shar
entries.content: [ Shar, the Mistress of the Night, is a greater goddess of darkness and the caverns of Faerûn, as well as a neutral evil greater deity. Counterpart to her twin Selûne, she presides over caverns, darkness, dungeons, forgetfulness, loss, night, secrets, and the Underdark. Among her array of twisted powers was the ability to see everything that lay or happened in the dark. Shar was also the creator of the Shadow Weave, which was a counterpart and attack upon the Weave.]

entries.name: Auril
entries.content: [ Auril, also known as The Cold Goddess, is the embodiment of winter's wrath. She is arrogant, capricious and unpredictable. She takes great pleasure in torturing her enemies and harassing her foes. Sacrifices and worship to her are often done out of fear. An evil goddess, her main goal is to cover the Realms under ice and snow.]

entries.name: Myrkul
entries.content: [ Myrkul, also known as the Lord of Bones, the Lord of the Dead and the Reaper, is the god of the dead in the Faerûnian pantheon. The avatar of Myrkul appears as a skeleton of a man hidden in flowing black robes. His wrinkled, lesioned skin and blackened, cracked lips give the appearance he was just on the verge of death. He speaks in a rather high whisper, though his words never show enough inflection to convey feeling or concern. He had mastered the skill of sparking unease and fear.]

entries.name: Mask
entries.content: [ Mask, the Lord of Shadows, was the god of shadows and thieves in the Faerûnian pantheon. He was a loner god most often associated with thieves or those of otherwise ill-repute. Known for his constant scheming, cool head, and oft-reserved biting comment he lost a significant portion of his power, the intrigue portfolio, to Cyric.]

entries.name: Blibdoolpoolp
entries.content: [ Blibdoolpoolp, also known as the Sea Mother, is the primary deity worshiped by the kuo-toa. Her holy symbol is a lobster head or a black pearl. Blibdoolpoolp usually takes the form of a 15‑foot-tall (5‑meter) nude human female, with a lobster's head and claws. Blibdoolpoolp is filled with hatred for the pain her kuo-toa children suffer at the hands of many races. A special enmity is held for surface-dwelling races, as well as illithids and drow.]

entries.name: Abbathor
entries.content: [ Abbathor, also known as the Great Master of Greed, was the dwarven god of greed before becoming an exarch of Bane. He is an intensely greedy deity and both desirous and envious of others' riches. Abbathor and his followers believe in the acquisition of all forms of wealth by any and all means necessary.]

entries.name: Velsharoon
entries.content: [ Velsharoon. the Archmage of Necromancy, also known as Mellifleur, is the Faerûnian god of necromancy.]

entries.name: Luthic
entries.content: [ Luthic was the orc goddess of caves and the mate of Gruumsh. She is the orc deity of fertility, medicine, females and servitude and often referred to as the Cave Mother. Luthic is the lesser orc deity of fertility, medicine, orc females, caves, wisdom, healing, and servitude. Her holy symbol is an orcish rune meaning "home".]

entries.name: Lathander
entries.content: [ Lathander, whose title was The Morninglord, is a deity of creativity, dawn, renewal, birth, athletics, spring, self-perfection, vitality and youth. He favores those who dispel the undead and blesses those who plant new life. Lathander is also the god called upon to bless birth and fertility related ceremonies.]

entries.name: Chauntea
entries.content: [ Chauntea is the Faerunian goddess of life and bounty, who viewed herself as the embodiment of all things agrarian. The Earthmother is seen as the tamer parallel of Silvanus, The Forest Father of druidry and wilderness, as she is the deity of agriculture and plant cultivation.]

entries.name: Mielikki
entries.content: [ Mielikki, also referred to as the Forest Queen, is the goddess of autumn, druids, dryads, forests, forest creatures, and rangers. Her symbol is a gold-horned, blue-eyed unicorn's head facing left.]

entries.name: Eldath
entries.content: [ Eldath, also known as The Green Goddess or Mother Guardian of Groves, is a lake spirit who acts as the guardian of groves and watersheds. Her presence is felt wherever there is calm. Eldath is a pacifist who avoids hostile action, even if threatened. Although shy, quiet and enigmatic, the Green Goddess is possessed of unknown depths of character and unexpressed resolve that could not be broken. Eldath protects rivers, streams, and druids' groves.]

entries.name: Deneir
entries.content: [ Deneir, often called the Scribe of Oghma, is the deity of art, cartography, glyphs, images, knowledge, literature and scholars.]

entries.name: Milil
entries.content: [ Milil, also known as the One Who Watches While Music is Alive and the Guardian of Singers and Troubadours, is the exarch of Oghma. He is predominantly worshiped by human, elf, and half-elf bards but attracts other musically-inclined individuals such as troubadours or poets. Milil is a consummate performer and possesses a confident, constantly-inspired personality. He possesses an impeccable memory as well as a broad knowledge of lore.]

entries.name: Silvanus
entries.content: [ Silvanus is the Faerunian god of nature, and one of the oldest and most prominent gods in the pantheon.]

entries.name: Oghma
entries.content: [ Oghma, also known as The Lord of Knowledge, is the neutral greater power of bards, inspiration, invention, and knowledge in Faerûn. Oghma is the leader of the Deities of Knowledge and Invention and his home plane is the House of Knowledge.]

entries.name: Gond
entries.content: [ Gond, known as Nebulen among gnomes and as as Zionil in the Shining Lands, is the Faerûnian god of craft, smithing, and inventiveness. The Lord of All Smiths pushes for innovation and imaginativeness, sometimes to a dangerous degree as a result of his short-sighted desire to create.]

entries.name: Waukeen
entries.content: [ Waukeen is a lesser deity of the Faerûnian pantheon known as the Merchant's Friend, Liberty's Maiden, and the Golden Lady. Her portfolio includes everything related to commerce and the accumulation of wealth through free and fair trade, as well as the beneficial use of wealth to improve civilization. Waukeen is portrayed as a slender, young woman with long, lustrous golden hair; always splendidly dressed. Waukeen was an active and enthusiastic deity who enjoyed the ebb and flow of goods.]

entries.name: Kossuth
entries.content: [ Kossuth, or the Lord of Flames was the god of elemental fire. Kossuth was symbolized by the holy symbol of a twining red flame. He is considered not to be a true god but actually an elemental primordial, a being whose power rivaled that of a true deity. Compared to the many other gods of Faerûn, Kossuth and the three other Elemental Primordials are well known for their relative silence when it comes to communication with their worshipers.]

entries.name: Asgorath
entries.content: [ Asgorath is the dragon deity of creation. He (or she, as some traditions suggested) is regarded as the creator of the multiverse and of dragonkind, and he manipulates the destinies of all dragons by operating in a way that nobody suspects his involvement. Asgorath is supposed to encompass all alignments, but is often regarded as neutral. In the Outer Planes, he is more commonly known as Io. Asgorath never manifests himself before his worshipers.]

entries.name: Akadi
entries.content: [ Akadi, the Queen of Air, is the embodiment of the element of air and goddess of elemental air, speed, and flying creatures. As an immortal being of freedom and travel, she instructs her followers to move as much as possible from place to place and from activity to activity.]

entries.name: Annam All-Father
entries.content: [ Annam All-Father is the chief giant deity and creator of the giant race, known also as the Prime, the Progenitor of Worlds, the Great Creator, and the Creator-By-Thought. Annam's avatar appears as a giant of massive size, standing at least 100 feet (30 meters) tall if not taller. He has white hair and a large full beard, and is clad in robes of midnight blue. Annam has a dual nature. He is an omniscient god of learning and meditation but can also act on impulse and instinct.]

entries.name: Celestian
entries.content: [ Celestian the Far Wanderer is an enigmatic deity from the world of Oerth revered by planewalkers and wildspace wanderers. He is one of the major powers worshiped on the Rock of Bral. He is also called the Star Wanderer. Celestian is portrayed as an older, black-skinned man who travels the skies. His dark eyes—the same color as his smooth skin—are full of knowledge. Celestian is tall and dressed in black robes covered in stars.]

entries.name: Asmodeus
entries.content: [ Asmodeus is the Faerûnian deity of indulgence and ruler of all devils. Asmodeus is a patron of oppression and power, the greatest devil, the Lord of the Ninth and overlord of the Nine Hells as a whole. Asmodeus's true form was that of a wingless scaled serpent hundreds of miles long. His form's sheer size makes it impossible for him to meet and enter into conversations with others. Therefore, he created humanoid-looking avatars. The location of his body is kept secret from everyone.]

entries.name: Tiamat
entries.content: [ Tiamat is the lawful evil dragon goddess of greed, queen of evil dragons and, for a time, a reluctant servant of the greater god Asmodeus. Tiamat is also the eternal rival of her brother Bahamut, ruler of the good metallic dragons. Tiamat is  a unique chromatic dragon, who has one head for each primary color of the most common species of chromatics.]

entries.name: Bane
entries.content: [ Bane is the Faerunian god of tyrannical oppression, terror, and hate, known across Faerûn as the face of pure evil through malevolent despotism. From his dread plane of Banehold, the Black Hand acts indirectly through worshipers and other agents to achieve his ultimate plan to achieve total domination of all Faerun. When summoned, Bane has a dark and rather shadowy appearance with a resemblance of dark armor and his tell-tale jeweled, dark gauntlet.]

entries.name: Bhaal
entries.content: [ Bhaal, known as Niynjushigampo among his Gugari worshipers, is the widely feared, Faerûnian god of violent and ritualistic murder. A wholly evil, debased and sadistic god, Bhaal was reviled by a majority of the pantheon.]

entries.name: Gargauth
entries.content: [ Gargauth, or The Lord Who Watches, is the lawful evil demigod of betrayal, cruelty, political corruption and powerbrokers. He embodies the inevitable decay and corruption that accompanies all self-serving, greedy, and power-hungry leaders and groups. Gargauth appeares as a fanged and clawed humanoid with horns and jagged shards of bone jutting out of his face and back.]

entries.name: Loviatar
entries.content: [ Loviatar, also known as The Maiden of Pain and The Willing Whip, is the evil goddess of agony and both queen and servant to the greater god Bane. Loviatar is a cold-hearted bully, calculating and despotic.  Loviatar was a servant of Bhaal and had a heated rivalry with her fellow servant Talona. During that time she often teased and tormented the goddess.]

entries.name: Talona
entries.content: [ Talona, called the Lady of Poison, Mistress of Disease, and Mother of All Plagues, is the goddess of poison and disease. Talona is depicted as an old crone who brought misfortune and death. On the other hand, she is also depicted to be a beautiful and innocent woman. Talona was a servant of Bhaal and had a heated rivalry with her fellow servant Loviatar. During that time she was often teased and tormented by her.]

entries.name: Tempus
entries.content: [ Tempus, also known as the Lord of Battles, is the god of war. His dogma is primarily concerned with honorable battle, forbidding cowardice and encouraging the use of force of arms to settle disputes. Faerûn is a violent land, and thus from sheer number of worshipers, Tempus was one of the mightiest deities in the Realms.]

entries.name: Leira
entries.content: [ Leira, also known as The Lady of Deception or The Lady of the Mists, is the goddess of deception and illusions and patroness of illusionists and liars. She is an enigma, never telling the truth when falsehood would do. Everything she does and said was shrouded in layers of illusion and lies. She believes that truth was worthless and that misbelief and falsehood are what gave life meaning.]

entries.name: Hyrsam
entries.content: [ Hyrsam, the Prince of Fools, is an ancient and powerful satyr archfey. He is a mischievous trickster who uses guile and savagery to further his goals. He is handsome, with a wild mop of curly hair, dark, intelligent eyes, and a fair face. Though he outwardly presented himself as a fool, Hyrsam was exceedingly clever and manipulative, with a streak of vicious savagery. Hyrsam was essentially an anarchist who opposed the influence of civilization on the Feywild.]

entries.name: Garagos
entries.content: [ Garagos, the Lord of War, was a god of war and exarch of Tempus, though he focused more on destruction than war itself. Garagos was far more heedless than Tempus in what war wrought, reveling in destruction and slaughter while the greater deity valued honorable combat.]

entries.name: Uthgar
entries.content: [ Uthgar, the Battle Father, is the god of physical strength, and the patron deity of the Uthgardt barbarian tribes. As a god, Uthgar was known for his competitive nature in combat and tireless ethic for training and tactics. He truly enjoyed everyday pleasures such as coupling, eating, drinking, hunting, or the camaraderie of another warrior.]

entries.name: Shaundakul
entries.content: [ Shaundakul, the Rider of the Winds, is the Faerûnian lesser deity of traveling and travelers, exploration, caravans, the wind as well as mining and miners. Lord Ao gifted him with portals and portal-walking. He manifests bodily as a bearded man who wears a traveler's cape and is armed with a greatsword called the Sword of Shadows.]

entries.name: Hlal
entries.content: [ Hlal is the dragon goddess of humor, inventiveness, and pleasure. Of all the dragon gods, she was the most friendly to non-dragons, and her symbol, a single white flame, represented the light of wit. In the Outer Planes she was more commonly known by the name of Aasterinian. Hlal manifests in whatever form suit her purposes at any given moment. Hlal delights in wordplay and sophisticated humor, and she is playful, stubborn and vain. She enjoys being shocking and innovative.]

entries.name: Selûne
entries.content: [ Selûne, also known as Our Lady of Silver, the Moonmaiden, and the Night White Lady, is the goddess of the moon in the Faerûnian pantheon. In both her avatars and her religious artwork, Selûne appears in many forms, like the phases of the moon. Again like the cycles of the moon, Selûne has many and changing moods and natures. Her faithful, coming from many walks of life, view her in countless different ways, and she reflects this. She is generous and freely bestows gifts and blessings on mortals.]

entries.name: Eilistraee
entries.content: [ Eilistraee is the drow goddess of beauty, song, dance, freedom, moonlight, swordwork, and hunting, within the drow pantheon known as the Dark Seldarine. She is the patroness and protector of the few dark elves who long to return to the surface and live there, at peace with other races. As an avatar, Eilistraee appears as a drow female of glowing beauty. Overall, the Dark Maiden's appearance inspires utter awe and astonishment, as well as emotions so deep to move mortals to tears.]

entries.name: Corellon
entries.content: [ Corellon, whose titles include Creator of the Elves and the Protector, is the patron god of all elves. Corellon used to be able to call many forms his true form but fixated his to that of a male sun elf. While Corellon shares the elven trait of pride that may border arrogance, this never gets the better of him. He is a god with an endless willingness to learn from others and acts on it.]

entries.name: Tymora
entries.content: [ Tymora, or more commonly Lady Luck, is the goddess of good fortune. She shines upon those who take risks and blesses those who deal harshly with the followers of Beshaba. Should someone flee from her sister's mischievous followers or defile the dead, their fate would be decided with a roll of Tymora's dice.]

entries.name: Beshaba
entries.content: [ Beshaba, or Lady Doom as she is also known, is the intermediate deity of accidents, bad luck, misfortune, and random mischief and a member of Tempus' pantheon. She demands worship to keep her bad luck at bay. Her aim in life is to destroy her sister Tymora, or Lady Luck. She also delights in cursing others, often causing seafarers to lose their navigational instincts.]

entries.name: Sune
entries.content: [ Sune, also known as Lady Firehair, is the deity of beauty, with governance also over love. Her dogma primarily concerns love based on outward beauty, with primary importance placed upon loving people who respond to the Sunite's appearance. When Sune appears to the mortals of Faerûn she wears only a near-transparent gown. She is known for her lustrous red hair that draped down to the ground, her eyes of shining emeralds and ruby red plump lips.]

entries.name: Sehanine
entries.content: [ Sehanine Moonbow, also called Daughter of the Night Skies, Goddess of Moonlight, and Lady of Dreams is an elven goddess of death, dreams, heavens, journeys, moon (full moon to be precise), moon elves, stars, and transcendence as well as the most powerful female member of the Seldarine. In her avatar form, Sehanine Moonbow looks like a 5 ft. tall youthful, ageless, female elf clad in a diaphanous gown, that looks like it is made of moonbeam.]

entries.name: Valkur
entries.content: [ Valkur, the Captain of the Waves, is an exarch of Tempus, patron of sailors, ships, favorable winds, and naval combat. Valkur's philosophy often puts him in conflict with the capricious ocean-goddess Umberlee and he is a sworn enemy of the Deities of Fury. He is friendly with Selûne, who guides sailors across the sea.]

entries.name: Umberlee
entries.content: [ Umberlee, also known as the Bitch Queen, is the evil sea goddess in the Faerûnian pantheon, most often worshiped by sailors or people traveling by sea, out of fear of her destructive powers. She is known as a particularly malicious, petty, greedy, and vain deity who controlls the harshness of the sea while reveling in her own power and is not hesitant to drown people if she so pleases.]

entries.name: Deities of Fury
entries.content: [ Gods of Fury was a collective term for a group of evil and destructive deities led by Talos, the Destroyer. The Gods of Fury were Talos, plus Auril, the Frostmaiden, Malar, the Beastlord, Umberlee, and the Bitch Queen.]

entries.name: Talos
entries.content: [ Talos, also known as The Storm Lord and long ago as Kozah, is  the Faerûnian greater deity of storms and destruction. His dogma is self-serving, demanding utter obedience from his priests and instructing them to spread destruction where they might. Talos appeares as a broad-shouldered, bearded man with one good eye. He wears half-plate armor over black leather and black leather gloves. His empty eye socket is filled with whirling stars and covered with a dark eye patch.]

entries.name: Malar
entries.content: [ Malar, The Beastlord, is the lesser deity of the hunt, evil lycanthropes, bestial savagery and bloodlust. His dogma concerns savage hunts, the spreading of the curse of lycanthropy, and general contempt for civilization. He is one of the Deities of Fury, led by Talos.]

entries.name: Lolth
entries.content: [ Lolth, or Lloth in Menzoberranzan, known as the Queen of Spiders or the Queen of the Demonweb Pits, is the most influential goddess of the drow, within the pantheon of the Dark Seldarine.]

entries.name: Dark Seldarine
entries.content: [ The Dark Seldarine, the pantheon of the drow, is "led" by Lolth, the Spider Queen, in the sense that she is the most powerful and widely worshipped drow deity.]

entries.name: Seldarine
entries.content: [ The Seldarine (Elvish for "fellowship of brothers and sisters of the wood") is the elven pantheon of gods that resides on the astral dominion of Arvandor under the leadership of Corellon Larethian.]

entries.name: Faerûnian pantheon
entries.content: [ The Faerûnian pantheon is the most worshiped pantheon on Faerûn, a continent on Toril.]

entries.name: Netherese pantheon
entries.content: [ The Netherese pantheon is pantheon of deities worshiped by those of the ancient Netherese Empire.]

entries.name: Orc pantheon
entries.content: [ The orc pantheon consists of the various gods of the orcs. They reside on the plane of Nishrek.]

entries.name: Draconic pantheon
entries.content: [ The draconic pantheon is the dragon pantheon of gods.]

entries.name: Cyric
entries.content: [ Cyric, known as Sirhivatizangpo by his Gugari worshipers and as N'asr by the Bedine, is the monomaniacal Faerûnian god of strife and deception, and the greater god of conflict and murder, as well as lies, intrigue and illusion. Cyric is petty, self-centered, and enjoys manipulating individuals into ruining or ending their own lives.]

entries.name: Demogorgon
entries.content: [ Demogorgon is a powerful demon lord and lesser deity from the Abyss. He is known to most as the Prince of Demons, and referred to as the Imprisoned One by some followers of Helm. He is huge, his body at once sinuous like that of a snake and powerful like that of a great ape. Two baleful baboon heads, each with its own personality, leer from atop his lumbering shoulders. His lower torso is saurian and he has an immense forked tail.]

entries.name: Baphomet
entries.content: [ Baphomet is a demon lord who rules a layer of the Abyss called the Endless Maze. He is the Prince of Beasts and the Demon Lord of Minotaurs. Baphomet has the appearance of a tall humanoid with a bull's head, a bovine tail, and broad, stubby hands and feet. His body is covered with coarse black hair. His horns curve downward and outward. He wields a giant bardiche.]

entries.name: Great Mother
entries.content: [ The Great Mother, sometimes specified as the Great Beholder Mother, is the eldritch matron deity of the beholders. Her title simply refers to her role as their progenitor rather than as an indicator of her questionable gender. Beholders themselves lack a name for her and feel no need to give her one. Those that study the Great Mother typically conclude that she is completely insane, lacking in the ruthless logic possessed by mortal beholders.]

entries.name: Lord Ao
entries.content: [ Lord Ao, known as the Hidden One or the One Who Is Hidden, is the Overgod of the worlds of Abeir-Toril. As Overgod, all deities and primordials of Abeir and Toril, even those who also operated in other spheres and planes, such as Lolth, are subject to him. Ao doesn't care what the deities are doing as long as they uphold their individual portfolios and do not completely ignore their worshipers. Ao's only job is to ensure deities abide by the rules of the cosmos, reporting to a "luminous being".]

entries.name: Luminous being
entries.content: [ The luminous being is a mysterious entity that exists beyond the normal cosmology, at the beginning and the end of time simultaneously, yet outside time and space proper. The luminous being is a cold and harsh entity, yet at the same time forgiving and warm.

entries.name: Sarenrae
entries.content: [Sarenrae, the Everlight, also known as the Dawnflower, the Healer and the Mother of Music, is the Divine of the Albionic Pantheon and patron of beauty, compassion and redemption. Her message is one of understanding and optimism in even the darkest of places. She believes the corrupt can be redeemed, a mindset that led to a betrayal by the Lord of the Hells that left most of her following destroyed in the Calamity. Only in recent centuries has her faith been rediscovered, coinciding with a revival of culture and the arts, and her temples returned to prominence. The Everlight’s followers are often rural healers, battlefield clinicians and community philosophers, becoming a voice of reason and empathy in angry and cynical times. The Everlight is most invoked during times of war, symbolising restoration of the wounded and comforting of the oppressed and displaced. Those who rise to bring her words back to the light unearth her image from ruined temples, or create new art to inspire others with her message. The Everlight is represented as a beautiful, strong woman of light skin and dark hair, always dressed in modest, working clothes. The Everlight’s original holy day has been long forgotten, and her followers have yet to decide when her festival should be held, and what the festivities should be. The debate has gone on for years, and no great miracles have yet been performed to unify the squabbling clerics.]

entries.name: Garl Glittergold
entries.content:
The gnome god of luck, protection and trickery, lawful good. Associated domain(s): Trickery.
The Watchful Protector is the king of gnomish gods - a deity of humour, gemcutting, protection, and trickery.

entries.name: Gruumsh
entries.content:
The patron deity of orcs and head of the orc pantheon, chaotic evil. Associated domain(s): Tempest, War.
The One-Eye is the orcs' patron deity - a god of war, conquest, and victory at all costs. He has led an ancient and immutable grudge against the elven pantheon since Corellon Larethian took his eye.

entries.name: Ilmater
entries.content:
The god of endurance and suffering, lawful good. Associated domain(s): Life, Twilight.
The Crying God protects the oppressed and persecuted. His clergy is sworn to alleviate suffering, even if that means taking on that pain personally.

entries.name: Kereska
entries.content:
The dragon goddess of magic and magical creativity, chaotic neutral. Associated domain(s): Arcana.
Kereska, draconic goddess of arcane knowledge, imbues many chromatic dragons with their magic, including their breath.

entries.name: Warforged
entries.content: [Warforged were a rare race of humanoid constructs created through powerful rituals. Warforged averaged 6′‒6′6″ (1.8‒2 m) and were made up of bulky (albeit resilient) metallic or stone bodies that weighed roughly 270‒300 lb (120‒140 kg).  Extremely powerful and durable, warforged were able fighters. Unlike most constructs, warforged were fully self-aware and maintained mental faculties on par with elves, humans, or similar races.]

entries.name: Aarakocra
entries.content: [also called bird-men, were a race of avian humanoids. Aarakocra were generally peaceful creatures who cherished their solitude. They were known to be extremely claustrophobic, often refusing to enter caves or other enclosed spaces. Male aarakocra tended to have very short tempers and had been known to fly into fits of rage when a perceived wrong occurred. They also were notorious romantic flirts, regardless of whether or not they were married.]

entries.name: Tabaxi
entries.content: [Tabaxi are feline humanoids, often described as catfolk, known for their agility, curiosity, and stealth. Originating from the distant jungles, tabaxi are natural explorers, driven by a wanderlust that compels them to seek out new experiences and knowledge. They are exceptionally fast and nimble, capable of scaling walls and traversing difficult terrain with ease. Tabaxi are often roguish in nature, preferring to live by their wits and reflexes rather than brute force, and they often seek out treasures or ancient lore as they travel. Tabaxi have short fur that is only centimeters above their skin, half of all tabaxi don't have fur tho, only having fur on their ears and tails. the fur usually has a plethora of unique patterns on it, usually being black, grey, orange, white, brown, and even blue, purple and red. all tabaxi have hair on their heads like humans, their ears sprouting out from it, tabaxi with no fur have eyebrows as well. tabaxi have soft hands and feet, they are silent when walking and are great climbers, they have the greatest reflexes out of any race. it is quite rare for tabaxi to be muscular, usually having thin, lithe frames, but it is something that can happen, a mutation that happens more in females, while normal tabaxi usually only grow up to around 5 feet tall, these muscular tabaxi can grow up to 7 feet tall, all while keeping their agility and reflexes, they have long claws and wilder hair and fur, they sleep much more than normal tabaxi. tabaxi females have human like genitalia, while males and Futanaris have spiked penises that can grow up to 9 inches in normal tabaxi and 13 inches in mutated tabaxi. the mutated tabaxi are called "tabaxi maxima".]

entries.name: Aetherborn
entries.content:
[Aetherborn come into being spontaneously as part of the aether refinement process. Their bodies and minds are apparently formed out of some interaction between the volatile elements of aether that are removed during refinement and the psychic impressions created by the people involved in the process. But each aetherborn is a unique individual, not a mere copy of some other person’s mind and shape. This race is little understood, and few aetherborn are willing to waste any of their short lives allowing vedalken scholars to study their biological and psychological characteristics.
Aetherborn are a strange living by-product of the process of aether refinement, cast in humanoid form but lacking any of the biological qualities of other races. They don’t eat or sleep, and they don’t reproduce—nor do they have any physical sexual characteristics. Language that categorizes people into male or female categories thus breaks down when it comes to aetherborn. Most aetherborn prefer that others use the pronoun “they” to refer to them, since it doesn’t attribute a gender that they don’t possess. Only a relative few prefer “he” or “she,” having chosen to adopt a gender.]

entries.name: Astral Elf
entries.content: [Astral Elves were a variety of elves native to the Astral Plane. They traced their roots to the Feywild like other elves, but were very different from their terrestrial brethren. The millennia they spent within the Astral Plane imbued them with a spark of divine energy, bestowed upon them by divine powers.]

entries.name: Autognome (Race)
entries.content:
[Autognomes are mechanical beings built by rock gnomes. Sometimes, because of a malfunction or a unique circumstance, an autognome becomes separated from its creator and strikes out on its own.
An autognome bears a resemblance to its creator, and most autognomes are programmed to speak and understand Gnomish. The internal components used in an autognome’s manufacture can vary wildly; one autognome might have an actual beating heart in its chest cavity, while another might be powered by stardust or intricate clockwork gears. Like gnomes, autognomes can live for centuries, typically up to 500 years.]

entries.name: Centaur (Race)
entries.content:
[The centaur was a large creature that lived in temperate forests. They could live solitary lives or live in small tribes. Centaurs were a strong and proud race. Although they typically strove to find peace and balance with nature, they could act with violence when the need arose. Despite this desire for balance, centaurs had to eat a lot to fuel their large bodies and were known to overindulge, especially with wine and ale. A drunken centaur was much more prone to aggressive and violent behavior.
Although some were solitary, centaurs generally lived in tribal hunter-gatherer societies. Those that felt a sense of wanderlust to explore the world made excellent companions, and occasionally would offer a ride to allies. The suggestion that they be used as a pack animal however would be met with derision. Centaurs had a strong hatred towards dracotaurs.]

entries.name: Changeling
entries.content: [Changelings are shape-shifters capable of altering their appearance at will, making them masters of disguise and subterfuge. Their fluid identities and mutable forms allow them to fit into almost any society, often taking on multiple personas. They are naturally adept at deception and stealth, making them ideal spies and diplomats. While some view changelings with suspicion due to their deceptive nature, others see them as versatile and adaptable individuals who can navigate complex social landscapes with ease. They have no genitalia but can create one on their body do to their shapeshifting abilities.]

entries.name: Dhampyr
entries.content: [Dhampyrs, also known as daywalkers and sometimes dhampirs, were living creatures who had inherited some of the tainted blood of vampires Dhampyrs were thin and willowy, with pale skin and slightly pointed ears. They had slightly pronounced canines and blood-red eyes. Dhampyrs were unharmed by sunlight or positive energy the way true vampires were. Many dhampyrs felt the characteristic bloodlust of a vampire as well as the ability to feed off of blood for sustenance or healing, though their thirst was much milder than that of true vampires and not all or even most dhampyrs carried out the practice.]

entries.name: Eladrin
entries.content:
[The term "eladrin" referred to a family of fey races or to specific races or subraces in that larger family. The larger family of eladrin included: 
-Fey eladrin, elven inhabitants of the Feywild,
-High elves, or "common" eladrin,
-Noble eladrin, powerful elf-like fey, and
-Celestial eladrin, a race of elf-like celestials.]

entries.name: Fey
entries.content: [There were many different species of fey, and connections between them could be hard to identify, other than being natives of the Feywild. A few common threads could be drawn between certain smaller groups, however, while some were simply impossible to classify. Some fey were strongly bound or associated with specific natural locations such as water bodies, landmarks, or other geographical features. These included dryads, hamadryads, nymphs, naiads, nereids, oreads, and fossergrim.]

entries.name: Firbolg
entries.content: [Firblogs were a reclusive race of giant-kin who preferred to avoid contact with other sentient races. They were both the most intelligent and the most powerful of the giant-kin]

entries.name: Genasi (Earth)
entries.content: [Earth genasi came in many physical shapes and appearances. Many carried obvious traits of the Elemental Plane of Earth, such as blocky features or earthlike skin, but others had earthlike features that were less apparent. Earth genasi were able to harness the power of the earth. They had darkvision and were able to pass over the ground without a trace. Earth genasi tended to be strong and tough, but were often stubborn and oblivious. They tended to be indifferent to others of their kind and thus in many cases isolated themselves. Earth genasi could be found anywhere. However, they were more common in the North near the Spine of the World, where there were portals to the Plane of Earth. A small population of earthsoul genasi lived in Mulhorand.]

entries.name: Genasi (Fire)
entries.content: [A fire genasi was a type of genasi that was able to harness the power of fire. Fire genasi were generally energetic and quick to act, and often impatient. They often cared a great deal about their appearance, and dressed flamboyantly. Fire genasi could summon nonmagical flame. They were also resistant to fire. Many fire genasi carried obvious traits from the Elemental Plane of Fire, such as coal-colored skin, flame-like hair, and fiery eyes.]

entries.name: Genasi (Water)
entries.content: [Water genasi were a type of genasi with elemental water ancestry. Like other genasi, water genasi looked generally human except for some distinguishing features, such as lightly scaled skin, clammy flesh, blue-green hair, excessive perspiration, blue-black eyes, or a muffled voice that sounds as if drowned in water. Compared with other genasi, water genasi were often slightly more durable, but also less strong. Most genasi had a lifespan identical to that of humans. Water genasi were unusually patient for genasi and had a strongly independent streak. Most were used to solving problems on their own and not afraid to take a lot of time doing so. At times they were like terrible storms, fierce and destructive, but most often they presented a tranquil appearance despite whatever emotions run underneath their quiet surface. Water genasi were often abandoned by their human parents and raised by aquatic creatures such as aquatic elves, dolphins, locathah, merfolk, sahuagin, or even aboleths. Water genasi usually leave their parents upon reaching maturity, taking to the open sea in order to explore, learn and develop their own personality and place in the world.  Many water genasi even looked down on humans who used the sea as their means to a livelihood, seeing them as vulnerable and weak fools. This brash arrogance means that, in general, water genasi did not get along as well with other races.]

entries.name: Genasi (Air)
entries.content: [Most air genasi are descended from djinn, air genies, though other origins exist, and the touch of the elemental power of wind and air shapes the genasi physique.
